title: Why property management LLCs need a high-reliability registered agent
summary: Protect your privacy and never miss critical legal notices. Learn why property management LLCs trust Stable for reliable agent services.
body_text: The right registered agent does more than keep your property management LLC compliant. It protects your privacy, keeps critical legal mail from falling through the cracks, and gives you the freedom to move between properties, meet with residents and vendors, and grow your portfolio without being tied to one office. ‍ Registered agents are a legal requirement for corporations and LLCs, but for property managers, the practical value goes well beyond checking a compliance box. A professional registered agent gives your team a reliable place to receive lawsuits and state notices while property managers are out conducting inspections, coordinating repairs, showing units, or meeting with owners and residents. ‍ Learn why you need a registered agent for your property management business . ‍ Not in property management? Our guide to registered agents for startups covers the same fundamentals for your startup. ‍ Key Takeaways ‍ A registered agent is a designated individual who can receive legal mail on your behalf, including legal correspondence and state mail. You can act as your own personal agent, but it comes with several risks including potential embarrassment and a lack of privacy. Property management LLCs hire professional agents to keep legal notices away from leasing offices and home addresses, stay reachable while teams are in the field, and support portfolios that span multiple states. Stable combines registered agent and virtual mailbox services to simplify business operations for property management companies. What is a registered agent? ‍ A registered agent is a designated individual who is responsible for receiving legal correspondence on behalf of your business. In order to be a registered agent, an individual must be at least 18 years old, be available during normal business hours, and have a physical street address in the state where the business is registered. ‍ You’re required to have a registered agent as an LLC or corporation. If your LLC or corporation is registered in multiple states, you must have a registered agent in each of the states you’re registered in. What do registered agents do for property management LLCs? Property management teams rarely spend every workday behind one desk. Between unit inspections, maintenance issues, resident meetings, vendor coordination, and owner reporting, a registered agent provides the fixed, reliable point of contact your LLC still needs for legal and state correspondence. For property management LLCs, that comes down to three core responsibilities: ‍ Service of process: Legal notices and subpoenas have to be officially served, and property managers can face claims involving residents, vendors, contractors, or incidents at a managed property. Your registered agent receives those documents at a designated address, so a process server does not have to arrive at your leasing office while your team is meeting with residents, owners, or prospects. ‍ State compliance and correspondence: Y ‍ our registered agent can receive state compliance correspondence on your behalf, including annual report reminders, state tax notices, and official filing mandates. That becomes especially useful as a property management company adds entities or expands into additional states, where notices may otherwise be scattered across different offices and addresses. ‍ Availability requirements: Registered agents maintain a strict presence at a physical street address during standard business hours (9:00 AM to 5:00 PM) to accept official deliveries. That requirement can clash with the day-to-day reality of property management, where your team may be walking units, overseeing a turn, responding to an emergency maintenance issue, or meeting a contractor across town. P.O. boxes cannot be used in place of a registered agent. Risks of being your own registered agent ‍ The law simply states that you have to designate a registered agent as an LLC or corporation, but you don’t have to hire a professional. You can be your own property management registered agent, but there are several risks. Exposure of personal address When you appoint a registered agent, the registered agent address appears in public state records. If you name yourself and use your home address, that can make your residence easier for residents, vendors, contractors, or other members of the public to find. ‍ For a property manager who handles sensitive situations such as disputes, evictions, security deposits, or vendor conflicts, keeping a personal residence separate from the business can provide an important layer of privacy. ‍ Hiring a professional registered agent gives your property management LLC a designated registered agent address instead of using your home address for that purpose. This keeps the privacy benefit focused where it belongs: on your public registered agent record. ‍ Your everyday business mail can still be handled separately through a business address or virtual mailbox. Potential embarrassing situations Property managers routinely meet with residents, prospective tenants, property owners, and vendors at leasing offices and management locations. If you use that same address as your registered agent address, a process server could arrive during one of those interactions in connection with a resident claim, vendor dispute, or other lawsuit. Even when the matter is routine, receiving service in a public-facing office can create an awkward and distracting situation for your team. ‍ Using a professional registered agent routes service of process to the registered agent’s designated address instead of your leasing or management office. Your team can still be notified quickly, but residents, prospects, and property owners do not have to witness a process server walking into the office. Lack of mobility A registered agent must be available at the registered office during standard business hours, which is a poor fit for many property management roles. A property manager may start the day at a move-in, head to an inspection, meet a roofer or plumber, and finish at another property handling a resident issue. Tying that person to one address just so the business can reliably receive official documents works against the way property management teams actually operate. ‍ Professional property management registered agents have one job: to stay in one place and receive mail on your behalf. You don’t have to worry about missing any important mail items, and your registered agent can notify you as soon as mail arrives. With Stable, registered agent mail is scanned, digitized, and made available in your dashboard, giving you instant visibility into time-sensitive documents. ‍ And missing a notice like this has real consequences. See the cost of registered agent non-compliance for what non-compliance can cost your business. ‍ A professional registered agent also prevents you from turning a leasing coordinator, office manager, or property manager into the person who has to stay behind just to receive official documents. That time can stay focused on resident communication, leasing activity, vendor coordination, owner reporting, and the dozens of operational issues that actually require your team’s attention. Why property managers hire professional registered agents ‍ For property management companies, the value of a professional registered agent has both operational and legal benefits. Your team gets a dependable point of contact for official documents without anchoring day-to-day property operations to a single office. That becomes more valuable as you add properties, entities, team members, and markets. Streamlined mail management Property management companies can receive mail from many directions: legal and state notices, owner correspondence, vendor invoices, insurance documents, checks, and everyday operational mail. When those items are landing at a leasing office, headquarters, or individual properties, staff can lose time opening, sorting, scanning, and routing them to the right person. Other property management companies are eliminating this bottleneck entirely. ‍ Stable brings registered agent services and virtual mailbox management together in one platform, eliminating the need to manage legal correspondence and everyday business mail through separate workflows. When you use Stable for both, your mail is aggregated into one unified dashboard and typically scanned and uploaded within one business day. Your team can then view mail remotely and request items to be opened, forwarded, or securely shredded — all without the overhead of maintaining a traditional mailroom. Privacy and discretion A professional registered agent lets you use the agent’s address for the registered agent listing on public state records instead of using a home or public-facing leasing office for that purpose. For property managers, that separation can matter when resident or vendor relationships become contentious: official legal deliveries go to the registered agent, while your home address stays out of that particular public filing. This is separate from everyday business mail, which can be managed through a business address or virtual mailbox. ‍ Using a registered agent service also helps route sensitive items such as tax notices, lawsuits, and state correspondence to the right people instead of leaving them on a front desk or in a shared leasing-office mail pile. ‍ With Stable, sensitive mail is digitized and stored in a secure dashboard, where access controls and permissions let you determine which team members can view and manage specific mail. A regional operator, legal contact, or finance lead can get visibility without requiring an onsite employee to scan and email the document manually. Multi-state scaling If your property management LLC is registered or qualified to do business in multiple states, it generally needs a registered agent in each of those jurisdictions. That can become an operational headache as a portfolio expands: entering a new market should not require finding a local employee or leasing office that can serve as the company’s permanent point of contact during business hours. ‍ A national commercial registered agent lets the same operations team support expansion without building a separate registered-agent workflow in every new market. If a management company adds a portfolio in another state, Stable’s coverage across all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico lets the team keep registered agent service centralized instead of sourcing and managing a different provider state by state. How to appoint or change your registered agent ‍ The process of appointing or changing your registered agent varies depending on whether you’re a new or existing LLC. ‍ If you’re starting a new LLC, you can name your registered agent directly on your Articles of Organization during your initial state filings. You’ll need the name of your registered agent, the street address, and their consent to act. ‍ If you have an existing LLC, you can file a Statement of Change of Registered Agent with your Secretary of State and pay the administrative filing fee to change your registered agent. Fees vary by state. If you’re switching from another provider, Stable can help with the Change of Registered Agent filing. How Stable optimizes property management compliance ‍ Stable doesn’t just offer property management registered agent services — we pair them with a virtual mailbox, digital mail management, deadline reminders, and prefilled compliance forms. ‍ That means a property management team can centralize registered agent correspondence alongside everyday business mail instead of relying on separate leasing offices or local staff to receive, scan, and forward documents. Time-sensitive mail is digitized in one dashboard, so the right operations, finance, or legal stakeholders can get visibility without waiting for a document to make its way from a property to headquarters. ‍ Plus, our coverage across all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico makes expanding to new markets easy without switching providers state by state. For a closer look at how registered agent and virtual mailbox service work together, see our full comparison guide . ‍ Talk to our sales team or compare Stable plans to get started. Frequently asked questions Can I be my own registered agent for my property management company? Yes, you can be your own registered agent for your property management company. However, acting as your own registered agent means exposing your personal or business address, potentially harming your reputation when lawsuits are served, and limiting your mobility during normal business hours. For a full breakdown of the pros and cons, see our post on whether you can be your own registered agent . Do I need a separate business entity or registered agent for each rental property? No. A registered agent is appointed for a business entity, not for an individual building or rental unit. If multiple properties are owned or managed through the same LLC, that LLC generally uses one registered agent in each state where it is registered or qualified. If your portfolio uses separate LLCs for different properties, each entity may have its own registered-agent requirement, so confirm the structure and state-specific rules with your legal or compliance advisor. What are the risks of using my home address for a rental business LLC? Using your home address as your registered agent address can make that address publicly available and expose your personal residence to tenants, vendors, or other members of the public. A professional registered agent lets you use the agent’s address for registered agent purposes instead, helping keep your home address private while ensuring official legal and state correspondence is reliably received. ‍

title: What is organic traffic? (And how to increase it)
summary: Organic traffic is the visitors who land on your site through unpaid search results. Increase yours in 5 steps.
body_text: There are a lot of factors that go into driving organic traffic, but the effort is worth it. It compounds over time, and unlike paid, it doesn't stop the moment you stop spending. The trick is knowing where to focus. Below, we'll cover what organic traffic is, its benefits and downsides, how AI search is affecting it, five steps to increase it, and how to check your results. What is organic traffic? Organic traffic refers to visits that come to your site via unpaid (i.e., "organic") search results. Meaning it's search engine traffic you get for free — aside from what it costs to create and maintain the content. Increasing organic traffic is one of the main goals of search engine optimization (SEO), because it brings in people already looking for what you offer. You get organic traffic when people click your website in the organic search results, or when they click your citation within Google’s AI Overviews or AI Mode . What are the benefits of organic website traffic? Organic traffic's core benefit is that it sends visitors to your site for free. Organic website traffic is also: Targeted : Organic traffic often attracts visitors who are specifically looking for the types of products/services and content you provide Sustainable : Organic traffic can provide a steady stream of visitors over time as long as your content remains relevant and optimized Scalable : You can increase organic traffic with an SEO and content marketing strategy But organic traffic also has potential downsides: Ongoing investments : Although organic traffic is free, you still need to invest in SEO and content marketing to improve your search engine visibility Slow growth : Organic traffic growth takes time, requiring consistent effort before you'll reliably see results Algorithm dependency : Organic traffic is dependent on search engine algorithms, which can change frequently Search engine results page (SERP) competition : Zero-click search features like AI Overviews and AI Mode absorb clicks that would have gone to organic results Organic vs. paid traffic While organic traffic visits come from appearing in standard search results, paid traffic visits come from pay-per-click (PPC) ads on results pages. Paid search campaigns deliver faster results and allow you to target users based on specific criteria, such as demographics, location, and search behavior. But these campaigns can be costly — especially in competitive markets. And the traffic stops as soon as you stop paying for ads. In contrast, organic search has the potential to generate clicks to your site as long as your content is live (and remains relevant and high-quality). You can estimate the total value of any website's organic traffic (the estimated monthly cost to rank for a website’s organic keywords in Google Ads) in Semrush's Organic Rankings tool. Just enter a domain and look for "Traffic Cost": Knowing a site's traffic cost tells you how much its owner would have to pay in Google Ads to replace the visibility it currently gets for free — useful for sizing up your own organic value or benchmarking a competitor's. How does AI search affect organic traffic? AI search has decreased organic traffic across most industries. Searchers now get detailed answers directly from AI systems like Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and ChatGPT, without needing to click through to a website. Apparel, beauty, food, and retail are the only industries of the 17 we analyzed that saw growth in organic traffic in 2025, according to our study on how AI is reshaping traffic channels . This doesn’t mean you shouldn’t focus on organic traffic. The same research found that organic search generated over 1 trillion visits in 2025, and AI traffic remains a fraction of that even after growing 66%. The signals that earn rankings also earn citations: accurate, well-sourced content on a site search engines can crawl. What's new is that AI systems rarely read a page start to finish. They pull the passage that answers the question. So pages built in clear, self-contained sections get cited more often than pages that bury the answer. And a reader who clicks your citation counts as organic traffic just like a reader who clicks a standard result. AI search optimization tools increase organic traffic by showing you where those citations are going. To see where you stand, Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit tracks how often your brand appears in AI-generated answers and which prompts your competitors are winning. Improving both rankings and citations starts with the same five steps. How to increase organic traffic Increase organic traffic by: Fixing any technical issues your site has so Google can access your content Finding keywords likely to drive organic traffic Creating optimized content that has a better chance of ranking high Acquiring backlinks to grow your site’s authority Setting up a Google Business Profile (if applicable) Let’s go over each step in greater detail. Step 1: Fix any technical issues your site has Fixing technical issues your site has ensures Google can discover, crawl, and index (store in a database) your website's content for you to rank for relevant queries and attract traffic. Semrush's Site Audit tool makes it easy to check your site for technical issues that could affect its crawlability and indexability . First, enter your domain into the text box and click " Start Audit ." Follow the prompts to configure your audit. When the audit is complete, you can see your site's overall health with the "Site Health" score. The higher the score, the fewer technical issues your site has. Head to the " Issues " tab to see a complete list of all the problems the tool detected. These are categorized into " Errors ," " Warnings ," and " Notices ." You should address errors first — they're the most severe issues affecting your site. In this example, the tool found broken JavaScript and CSS files, broken images, mixed content, and invalid structured data. Click " How to fix " next to any issue to learn how to address it. Take whatever steps you need to resolve the first error. Then, work through the rest of the errors, warnings, and notices. Further reading : How to Perform a Technical SEO Audit in 10 Steps Step 2: Perform keyword research Performing keyword research helps you identify the queries people use when searching for information related to your niche. Find relevant search terms with Semrush’s Keyword Magic Tool . Enter a seed keyword (a broad term related to your niche) into the text box and your domain in the field below it. Then, click " Search ." The tool will then produce a list of relevant keyword suggestions. It also provides important metrics for each keyword, including: Search intent (Intent) : What users are hoping to achieve when they perform a search for that term Search volume (Volume) : The average number of monthly searches for the keyword Personal Keyword Difficulty (PKD %) : The estimated ranking difficulty for that keyword on a scale of 0 to 100 for your specific domain. The lower the score, the more likely you are to rank well. Potential traffic : An AI-driven forecast that analyzes your domain and estimates your potential traffic from a given keyword, based on your domain's relevancy and Topical Authority Your goal is to find terms with the right combination of high potential traffic and low Personal Keyword Difficulty. And then target those terms with the right type of content to satisfy the searcher's intent. (More on that in the next step.) You'll find keyword groups (topically related terms) in the left-hand menu. Which can be useful for exploring more specific keyword topics within your niche. You can find more relevant keywords by seeing which terms your competitors target that you don’t. Use Semrush's Keyword Gap tool for this. Enter your domain and at least one competitor's domain. Then, click " Compare ." The tool will then compare the keyword profiles of each domain. The two keyword categories you should focus on first are: Missing : These are keywords your competitors rank for but you don't Weak : These are keywords your competitors rank for higher than you There's a good chance you'll find some great keyword opportunities here. After all, if your closest competitors are ranking for certain keywords, they're probably relevant to your website as well. Move on to the next step once you’ve selected keywords most likely to drive traffic to your site. Further reading : Keyword Research for SEO: What It Is & How to Do It Step 3: Create optimized content Optimized SEO content that satisfies users' needs is more likely to rank highly in organic search results and drive traffic to your site. It also helps you establish authority in your niche, build trust with your audience, and earn citations in AI-generated answers. The Content Optimization tool, available in both Enterprise AIO and Enterprise SEO, gives you tips for optimizing your content for organic and AI search. Start by creating a brief with the keywords you wish to target. You can write your article directly in the tool or copy and paste in an existing article (if you need to re-optimize one you’ve already published). Here are some tips to help you write content that ranks: Answer the query in your first sentence : Mirror the heading or target keyword so readers get an immediate, extractable answer Structure with clear H2s and H3s : Each heading should signal exactly what the section covers, so users can jump straight to it Keep sections self-contained : Write each section so it makes sense without needing context from earlier paragraphs, since AI systems often pull isolated chunks Back claims with data or sources : Cite research, stats, or first-hand experience instead of general statements to increase your odds of being cited Use short, direct sentences : Cut dependency hops so both readers and AI systems parse your point quickly As you write, apply the tips provided and aim to score as high as possible for AI SEO and SEO. Step 4: Build quality backlinks Building quality backlinks from other reputable websites increases your site's authority and credibility, which can lead to better rankings and more organic traffic. The key to building quality backlinks is to consistently publish high-value content that other sites naturally want to link to. Speed up this process with dedicated link building tactics . Some examples include: Unlinked brand mentions : Finding sites that mention your brand without linking to it, then asking them to add the link Checking competitor backlinks : Identifying sites that link to your competitors but not you, then asking them to link to yours as well Broken link building : Finding a site with a broken external link and offering a relevant, working resource on your own site as the replacement Find broken links with the Backlinks tool. Enter a rival’s domain and click “ Analyze .” Head into the “ Indexed Pages ” report and check off “ Broken Pages .” Now you have a list of your competitor’s broken pages. Look for a broken page similar to one you already have published, or one you could easily create content for. Then click “ # ” in the backlinks column to view which sites link to the broken page. Identify reputable and relevant sites and reach out to each one. Let them know they are currently linking to a broken page and offer your resource as a working replacement. Further reading : Link Building for SEO: A Guide to the Basics Step 5: Set up your Google Business Profile (if applicable) Setting up and maintaining your Google Business Profile (GBP) can increase your visibility for location-based searches if you run a brick-and-mortar business or a local service business. A GBP is a free business listing that shows important information about your business directly in the search results. It’s an important part of local SEO . Populate your GBP with as much relevant information as you can to maximize its visibility and persuade people to visit your site. Include: Your business description Your business category Your website, phone number, and address (or service area) Your business hours Photos of your business, products, or services Consistent information across the web helps search engines and AI tools verify that your details are accurate, which improves your visibility in both places. Then, keep your GBP active by asking customers for reviews (more reviews with high ratings can improve local rankings) and posting regularly. You can learn more about how to optimize your profile in our in-depth guide to GBP . How to check your site's organic traffic You can check your site's organic traffic using three tools: Semrush's Organic Rankings, GA4, and Google Search Console (GSC). Organic Rankings Follow these steps to use Semrush's Organic Rankings tool to see any website's organic traffic estimates: Enter a domain into the text box and hit " Search " View the "Traffic" number at the top of this report, which estimates how many monthly visits organic rankings drive to the site Click the " Traffic " section to see an estimate of the domain's organic traffic over time Click on the " Position changes " report to see how ranking changes affect traffic Google Analytics 4 Follow these steps to check organic traffic in GA4: Go to your GA4 account Click on " Reports " Under the "Life cycle" section, click " Acquisition " > " Traffic acquisition " Here, you can see all your traffic sources, including "Organic Search" To see the specific search engine driving your organic traffic, scroll down the "Traffic acquisition" report. Then, add "Session source" as a secondary dimension. Look for any spikes or drops in organic traffic. Investigate anomalies further to see why they may have happened. For example, a temporary drop in organic traffic could indicate an algorithm update. Review SERP volatility from Semrush Sensor to confirm. Further reading : What Is Organic Traffic in Google Analytics 4? (+ Analysis Tips) Google Search Console Follow these steps to check organic traffic with GSC: Go to your GSC account Open the " Performance " report. Here, you'll see the total number of organic clicks driving traffic to your site from Google's search results. Scroll down to see which queries, pages, and countries bring the most organic traffic to your site Re-optimize any search terms that are ranking lower than anticipated using the Content Optimization tool. Keep track of your organic traffic performance Keeping track of your organic traffic can support your business's long-term growth. And making technical improvements, doing keyword research, creating content, and building links are all vital ingredients for improving your organic visibility and traffic. As you work to improve your SEO efforts, use a tool like Enterprise SEO's Keyword Rankings Overview report to monitor your keyword rankings. Rankings move before organic traffic does, so they show whether your changes are working before the visits arrive. With Semrush Enterprise, you can also track rankings across AI search surfaces, so you can see how your visibility is shifting across the different places people go to find answers. Try it today.

title: A Retailer’s Guide to Returns Management Software in 2026
summary: Explore returns management software features, Shopify’s native tools, and an expert-backed framework for choosing the right platform.
body_text: Return volumes continue to grow. Per Statista Market Insights, 7.4% of global ecommerce revenue in 2025 was returned to store owners, and the figure is forecast to reach 9% by 2029. According to Radial, nearly half of shoppers say they’ll stop buying from a retailer that flags a genuine return as fraudulent. This leaves you in a bind: protect the margin, lose the customer; please the customer, lose the margin. To resolve this tension, treat each return on its own terms. This is something policy documents can’t do, but returns management software can. Ahead, learn why returns management solutions are increasingly important for customer engagement, plus the key capabilities you need to scale. What is returns management software? A returns management software solution applies your return rules to determine whether an item qualifies for a refund, exchange, or store credit. The platform can then generate a label, offer a refund or exchange, calculate fees, and keep the customer updated. Once the item comes back, it helps teams track its condition and decide whether to restock, repair, resell, recycle, or dispose of it. The category often gets confused with three adjacent systems that either sit upstream or downstream of it: Reverse logistics. A reverse logistics software solution handles what happens physically after a return is authorized. Your returns management software typically sits a layer above this; it owns the customer-facing decision of whether a return is eligible and what the customer gets back, then hands the physical movement to reverse logistics systems or a 3PL. Order management system (OMS). An OMS is built for the forward transaction: placing, processing, and fulfilling a purchase. It can integrate returns management software to keep inventory and orders in sync. Help desk. A help desk gives customers a place to ask about a return and gives agents a ticket to answer it. But it doesn’t enforce return policy automatically, check eligibility rules, flag fraud patterns, or route items to a warehouse. That means returns can belong to several teams at once. For instance, customer experience teams manage shopper questions and exceptions; ecommerce and operations teams set return rules and workflows; logistics and warehouse teams receive, inspect, and route products; finance reconciles refunds and fees; while fraud teams review suspicious behavior. Benefits of returns management software Returns management software helps owners protect margins, keep more customers, and reduce manual work. In 2026, it also helps businesses meet new customer experience and compliance expectations. Since June 19, 2026 , businesses selling online to consumers in the European Union have been required to offer a simple digital way for shoppers to cancel eligible purchases and exercise their right of withdrawal. The function must be easy to find, collect the required order details, and send the customer an electronic confirmation. Email and customer service can still support the process. But they can no longer be the only way customers exercise this right. The withdrawal option has to be built into the digital experience itself. A reason retailers are looking at this category now is compliance; it’s projected to grow to $8.53 billion by 2026. The bigger opportunity is operational, the right system can help businesses recover value, control costs, improve customer experience, and apply stronger fraud controls. But other than that, four pressures are converging on returns at once: Recover more value from returned inventory Returned products need both processing and a clear path back into the business. McKinsey estimates that retailers spend $200 billion each year trying to recover value from returned products. Software can make those decisions easier when returns move across warehouses, stores, markets, and third-party logistics providers. Protect margin beyond the refund The National Retail Federation (NRF) and Happy Returns estimated that retailers received $849.9 billion in returns from 2025 sales. Of those, online return rates were higher than the overall average, at an estimated 19.3% of ecommerce sales. Returns software helps reduce manual work and added costs tied to return shipping, inspection, customer support, restocking, and fraud and policy abuse. Make returns easier to keep customers coming back A smoother return experience can support loyalty. Radial found that 61% of consumers become less interested in shopping with a retailer if they have to pay return fees. It also found that up to 71% would rather keep an unwanted product and not buy from the brand again than deal with a frustrating return. Returns software helps reduce that friction with clearer workflows and faster resolution. Apply stronger controls as volume grows Manual review becomes harder to maintain as return volume increases. As ReBound returns product manager Wouter ten Heggeler says in Business Wire , that the returns process has become a blind spot for retailers. That’s why 44% of brands now call returns fraud and abuse their single biggest operational pain point, per Radial. Returns software can help businesses enforce policies more consistently and spot abuse earlier. If you’re on Shopify, a Built for Shopify–certified app like EU Withdrawal Button & Form builds the withdrawal button directly into checkout, without requiring your customers to log in, alongside broader return and exchange automation. The payoff, however, isn’t limited to just returns. Asphalte , a French apparel brand built on a pre-order model, resells surplus pre-order returns and cancellations through Le Magasin, their first permanent store. “We adopted Shopify for what it does best: the smooth processing of orders, exchanges, and returns, as well as its efficient payment process,” says Benjamin Mateo, chief revenue officer. Key features of the best returns management software G2’s Returns Management category sets six qualifying criteria a product must meet to be listed in the category at all. So, when comparing vendors, test each one against all six categories individually. 1. Configurable return policies The platform has to let you create and manage return policies for different product categories. That means the policy engine needs to flex across product type, order value, customer segment, and geography. Shopify’s return and cancellation rules cover this at the settings level. You set a return window—14, 30, 90 days, unlimited, or a custom number—and choose whether it starts from each item’s own delivery date or from delivery of the last item in the order. For sellers operating across regions, rules can be set per market instead of storewide. For example, if you’re selling to EU consumers, you can set a return window of at least 14 days from delivery of the final item, allow cancellations until fulfillment, and extend deadlines that fall on weekends or holidays. This supports the EU right-of-withdrawal requirements that took effect on June 19, 2026, although these Shopify settings do not, by themselves, guarantee legal compliance. 2. Self-service and automated return workflows G2’s second criterion covers workflows to create, confirm, or cancel a return—the mechanics of what happens after a request comes in. Shopify lets customers request cancellations for unshipped items and returns for delivered items through their customer account or order status page. On the automation side, Shopify Flow handles the bulk of the work. Shopify Flow triggers on the specific status a return is in— requested , approved , declined , cancelled , reopened , or closed —alongside the existing refund-created trigger. A cancel-return action pairs with these to handle returns that stall out, like when a customer says they’ll send an item back and never do. You can use these triggers to build workflows such as alerting a team in Slack when a customer requests a return, cancelling inactive returns after a set period, or releasing exchange items for fulfillment once the original return has been closed and the order has no outstanding balance. Take SilkSilky . The apparel brand used Shopify Flow for flagging high-risk orders and placing them on payment hold before fulfillment, so a team member could request partial card verification before the order shipped. The brand’s return rate fell from 7% to 8% to less than 1% as a result. 3. Flexible refunds, credits, and replacements G2’s third criterion is about coordinating refunds, credits, or product replacements. Shopify supports these options natively in the admin . Your staff can add an exchange or replacement item to a return, refund the customer to their original payment method, issue store credit, or split the refund between both. The store credit can also be given an expiry date. Shopify automatically works out the balance when the returned and replacement products have different values. Shopify’s Spring 2026 Editions extends this flexibility in stores. Refunds, exchanges, and new purchases can now run through one Shopify POS cart rather than separate transaction flows. Your staff adds the replacement or newly purchased products, and Shopify POS calculates whether the customer should receive a refund or pay the remaining balance. The same release adjusts two things on the admin side: Discounts can now be applied directly on the refund page , so a partial refund with a goodwill discount attached doesn’t throw off sales and tax reporting. Returns and upsells now calculate pricing the same way checkout does, so an exchange with a price difference charges the right amount automatically. 4. Commerce and operations integrations G2’s fourth criterion is integration with ecommerce or related platforms; integration deep enough to power capability that wouldn’t otherwise exist. G2 notes that returns platforms commonly integrate with ecommerce, order management, warehouse management, inventory, and accounting software. Princess Polly , for example, integrated Loop with Shopify so customers could use their return credit to select another product directly from its website. The integration passed data between the customer-facing return experience and back-office operations, while giving the brand returns insights and customer feedback. Princess Polly reported a 55% year-over-year reduction in out-of-stock rates through instant exchanges and an average upsell of $1.23 per return through Loop’s Shop Now feature. “Thanks to Shopify Plus and Loop, we’ve seen a huge improvement in our return experience, with customers telling us first-hand that they appreciate how easy it is. And not only is it improving our customer loyalty—it’s also driving a significant uptick in revenue,” says Alexandria Collis, director of operations. When comparing Shopify’s almost 200 returns and exchanges apps , look for the Built for Shopify designation. From December 1, 2026 , returns and exchange apps offering buyer-facing self-service must use Shopify’s Customer Account API to retain that status. This gives customers one secure sign-in across their account, storefront, and connected app rather than requiring a separate login for the returns portal. 5. End-to-end return tracking G2’s fifth criterion is tracking returned items from the moment they’re picked up to the moment they’re received. On the customer side, Shopify’s order status page updates in real time as a return moves through its stages. When something’s gone wrong in processing, rather than leaving the customer guessing, the return is flagged with a distinct “Return failed” status. Returns tracking works with hundreds of carriers automatically —DHL, UPS, FedEx, Canada Post, Australia Post, and EVRi among them—so this functionality isn’t limited to labels purchased directly through Shopify. On your side, Shopify assigns each order a return status : Return requested, Return in progress, Inspection complete, or Returned. You can filter orders by these statuses to find requests that need approval, returns awaiting processing, or refunds that still need to be issued. 6. Returns analytics and business impact G2’s sixth and final criterion is analyzing the value of returns and their impact on revenue. Shopify now uses category-specific return reasons across the admin, Shopify POS, self-serve returns, and compatible third-party apps. So, a footwear customer might select “too narrow,” while a beauty customer can report an issue with shade or coverage. You can then use those patterns in data to improve product descriptions and sizing guidance or work with suppliers on recurring quality issues. Shopify’s Analytics further connects those reasons to physical and financial return metrics. Merchants can review the quantity and percentage of units physically returned, the reason attached to each line item, and the value of sales reversals by product. Returns reduce net and total sales in Shopify’s sales reports , making their effect on revenue visible alongside the products that generated it. And because return reason data feeds into the same operational picture as sales and receiving data, you can ask Shopify’s AI assistant, Sidekick , direct questions—what’s not moving, what to reorder this week—and get an answer informed by why products are coming back. How do you choose the best returns management platform? While popular options in G2’s returns management category include Narvar, ReturnGO, ClickPost, parcelLab, AfterShip Returns, and Happy Returns, these platforms aren’t interchangeable. Some focus on self-service portals and workflow automation, while others extend into broader post-purchase communication, carrier management, physical drop-off networks, and reverse logistics. Decide whether you need another platform Before shopping for software, check what your commerce platform already supports. Shopify can manage return and cancellation rules, customer return requests, refunds, store credit, exchanges, return shipping information, inventory updates, and return-reason analytics natively. Shopify Flow can automate tasks when a return is requested, approved, declined, canceled, closed, or reopened. And Shopify’s rich network of apps and APIs extends the platform: “We have around 18% EBITDA margins, which is way above average for an apparel brand,” says SuitShop cofounder Diana Ganz . “We attribute much of this to the efficiencies enabled by Shopify and its ecosystem of apps.” A dedicated returns platform becomes more useful when: You need more advanced self-service exchanges and exchange incentives You manage complex routing across warehouses, stores, and 3PLs You need a large international carrier or physical drop-off network You run returns management across several ecommerce platforms Ask the same questions of every vendor Once you’ve answered the question of whether or not to add more software, use G2’s six category criteria to compare shortlisted platforms consistently: How configurable are your return policies? Can you set different windows, fees, eligibility rules, and final-sale exceptions by product, market, channel, or customer? What parts of the workflow can you automate? Can customers start a return themselves? Which requests can be automatically approved or declined? Can the platform generate labels, notify teams and customers, close inactive returns, and send unusual cases to an employee for review? Which resolutions do you support? Can you offer refunds, store credit, replacements, variant exchanges, or exchanges for another product? How well do you integrate with our operations? Check the vendor’s connections with your ecommerce platform, POS, order and inventory management systems, ERP, warehouse software, 3PLs, carriers, customer support tools, and accounting systems. Can you track the complete return? The platform should show what has happened from the initial request through shipping, receipt, inspection, restocking, exchange, and refund. What can you learn from the returns data? Look for return rates, reasons, product-level trends, processing times, shipping costs, refund value, exchange uptake, retained revenue, and inventory outcomes. The future of retail: why unified commerce is no longer optional New research shows businesses using unified commerce platforms like Shopify POS see 22% better total cost of ownership and 20% faster implementation. Learn what this means for your retail strategy. Get the report Returns management software FAQ What is return management? Return management is the returns process for receiving, reviewing, tracking, refunding, exchanging, and restocking returned products. Returns software can use automated workflows to approve requests, generate return labels, provide real-time tracking, and update warehouse management systems, which improves operational efficiency and increases customer satisfaction. How big is the return management market? Estimates vary because research firms define the category differently. The Insight Partners valued the global returns management software market at $1.58 billion in 2023 and projects it will reach $3.29 billion by 2031 . What is the difference between customer return and RTO? A customer return happens after an order has been delivered and the buyer sends it back. Return to origin (RTO) happens when delivery cannot be completed, so the carrier sends the parcel back to its original pickup location. What is the average customer return rate? US retailers estimated that 15.8% of sales would be returned in 2025. The rate for ecommerce returns was higher, at an estimated 19.3% of online sales, although rates vary by product category and retailer. What is RTO dropshipping? RTO dropshipping occurs when a supplier ships an order directly to the customer, but delivery fails, and the parcel returns to the supplier or fulfillment origin. Dropshippers may still pay outbound and return shipping costs, so order verification, fraud prevention, and AI-powered risk screening can help identify high-risk returns, mitigate risk, and support revenue retention. What is RTO and RVP in ecommerce? RTO, or return to origin, happens when an order cannot be delivered and is sent back to the seller. RVP, or reverse pickup, happens after delivery, when a carrier collects an item that the customer wants to return or exchange. Some logistics providers use different terms for this second journey, such as DTO. The best returns management solution should separate these flows so teams can analyze customer behavior, offer a flexible return resolution, and optimize returns. At higher support volume, automated updates can reduce support ticket volume, while fraud detection tools help flag fraudulent post-purchase activities.

title: Online Payment Methods Malaysia — Complete SME Reference 2026
summary: Every major online payment method for Malaysian SMEs: DuitNow QR, FPX, Touch ’n Go, GrabPay, BNPL, and cards — with T+2 MYR payouts.
body_text: Quick Answer: Malaysian SMEs can accept online payments across DuitNow QR, FPX, Touch ’n Go, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Boost, Atome, GrabPay PayLater, SPayLater, WeChat Pay, Alipay, and Visa/Mastercard cards. Each method serves a different customer segment and requires different gateway configuration. HitPay supports all of these methods for Malaysian merchants with no monthly fees and T+2 calendar day MYR payouts for domestic transactions. Malaysia’s e-commerce market is expanding rapidly. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia , digital commerce now accounts for a significant and growing share of retail activity — and customers in Bangsar, Bukit Bintang, and Johor Bahru increasingly expect to pay using their preferred e-wallet or bank app, not just a card. For SMEs, offering the right mix of payment methods is no longer optional. It directly affects conversion rates, cart abandonment, and repeat purchase behaviour. The challenge for most small businesses is not awareness — it is knowing which methods to prioritise, how to set them up without a monthly fee burden, and how quickly settlements will arrive in their bank accounts. What online payment methods do Malaysian customers actually use? Malaysia has one of the highest e-wallet adoption rates in Southeast Asia, driven by the national DuitNow infrastructure and a competitive e-wallet market. The Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) has identified cashless payments as a core pillar of Malaysia’s digital economy strategy, accelerating adoption across SMEs and consumers alike. Here is a breakdown of the key methods Malaysian merchants need to support online: Payment Type Method Notes QR / Instant DuitNow QR National standard; works across all major banks Bank Transfer FPX (Financial Process Exchange) Direct bank debit; widely used for higher-value purchases E-Wallet Touch ‘n Go, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Boost Top four by active user base BNPL Atome, GrabPay PayLater, SPayLater Growing fast in fashion, electronics, lifestyle Cards Visa, Mastercard Essential for international and B2B buyers Tourist / Cross-border Alipay, WeChat Pay Captures Chinese Malaysian and international shoppers For cross-border sales, Malaysian merchants can also accept PayNow (Singapore customers), QRIS (Indonesian customers), PromptPay and TrueMoney (Thai customers), and QR Ph (Filipino customers) — without needing a foreign entity. Cross-border transactions settle at T+2 in MYR. How does each major payment method work for online merchants? DuitNow QR is the foundational method — regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia and interoperable across all participating banks. Customers scan a QR code and authorise payment through their banking app. Settlement is fast and dispute rates are low. FPX (Financial Process Exchange) is a direct bank debit system. It is the preferred method for higher-value transactions — tuition fees, B2B invoices, software subscriptions — because it draws directly from the customer’s bank account with no card required. For a deeper look at FPX payment gateways in Malaysia , HitPay’s guide covers gateway options and integration approaches in detail. Touch ‘n Go is one of Malaysia’s most widely used e-wallets. HitPay’s direct integration with Touch ‘n Go offers a transaction fee of 1.9% for online payments — reduced from a previous 2.3% rate — and is auto-enabled for all Malaysia merchants upon sign-up. GrabPay and PayLater by Grab are available for both online and in-person payments. PayLater by Grab offers 1, 4, 8, or 12-month instalment plans with a customer credit limit of up to RM 6,000 — relevant for merchants selling furniture, electronics, or travel packages. Atome is a buy now, pay later (BNPL) option that splits purchases into 3 interest-free instalments. The minimum transaction is RM 10. BNPL options like Atome are documented to boost average order values by up to 30% in retail categories — for more context on BNPL options for Malaysian businesses , the full comparison covers fees, approval rates, and merchant terms. WeChat Pay is relevant for merchants in areas with high Chinese Malaysian foot traffic or tourist exposure. Over 70% of Chinese tourists in Malaysia prefer e-wallet payment methods. HitPay’s direct WeChat Pay integration supports both online QR and redirect flows. Alipay connects Malaysian merchants to 10+ international wallets — including Alipay CN, Alipay HK, GCash, Dana, Rabbit LINE Pay, and TrueMoney — making it the most efficient single integration for cross-border online sales. How do merchants set up online payments in Malaysia? Sign up for a payment gateway account (HitPay approval takes 1–3 business days; no setup fee required). Navigate to Settings > Payment Methods in the dashboard to enable the relevant methods. For methods requiring onboarding forms (Atome, Alipay), submit the form through the Payment Methods page; activation typically takes 3–5 business days. Touch ‘n Go, GrabPay, and DuitNow QR are auto-enabled for verified merchants — no additional form needed. Integrate with an online store or platform. HitPay supports Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, and direct API connections. Set payout preferences. Domestic MYR transactions settle in T+2 calendar days; cross-border transactions settle T+2. For merchants using payment links rather than a full storefront, payment links for Malaysian businesses can be created and shared via WhatsApp, email, or social media — without a website. What should merchants look for in a Malaysia payment gateway? Five factors matter most for Malaysian SMEs: Payment method coverage — does the gateway support DuitNow QR, FPX, Touch ‘n Go, GrabPay, ShopeePay, BNPL, and cards in a single integration? Fee structure — monthly fees erode margin at low volumes. Pay-per-transaction pricing is better for seasonal or growing businesses. Payout speed — T+2 calendar day MYR settlement is the benchmark for domestic transactions. Regulatory compliance — the gateway must operate within Bank Negara Malaysia’s payment system licensing framework. Cross-border support — merchants selling to Singaporean, Indonesian, or Thai customers need cross-border wallet acceptance without additional entities. HitPay supports 50+ payment methods for Malaysian merchants, charges no monthly or setup fees, and settles domestic transactions in MYR in T+2 calendar days. Pricing details are available at hitpayapp.com/pricing. The payment landscape in Malaysia will continue to evolve — Alipay added in October 2025, WeChat Pay direct integration launched September 2025, Touch ‘n Go moved to direct integration in August 2025. Merchants benefit from a gateway that keeps pace with these changes without requiring manual reintegration each time a new method launches. Frequently Asked Questions What is the most popular online payment method in Malaysia? DuitNow QR is the most widely adopted online payment method in Malaysia, operating as the national interbank QR standard regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia. FPX is the leading bank-transfer method for higher-value transactions, while Touch ‘n Go and GrabPay dominate the e-wallet segment by active user count. How do I start accepting online payments in Malaysia with no monthly fees? HitPay allows Malaysian merchants to sign up for free, with no monthly or setup fees. Merchants apply online, receive approval within 1–3 business days, and can immediately enable payment methods including DuitNow QR, FPX, Touch ‘n Go, GrabPay, ShopeePay, and Visa/Mastercard cards through the HitPay dashboard. Charges apply only per transaction. How fast are payouts for Malaysian merchants? Domestic MYR transactions processed through HitPay settle in T+2 calendar days. Cross-border transactions — such as payments from Singaporean customers via PayNow or Indonesian customers via QRIS — settle at T+2 in MYR. Can Malaysian merchants accept payments from overseas customers? Yes. Malaysian merchants can accept cross-border payments from customers in Singapore (PayNow), Indonesia (QRIS), Thailand (PromptPay, TrueMoney, Rabbit LINE Pay), the Philippines (QR Ph), and South Korea (KakaoPay, PayCo, LINE Pay) — all without a foreign entity. Alipay also enables acceptance from Chinese, Hong Kong, Indonesian, and Philippine wallet users through a single integration. Is BNPL worth offering for a Malaysian online store? BNPL is well-suited to merchants in fashion, electronics, lifestyle, and travel categories. Atome, GrabPay PayLater, and SPayLater are the three main options in Malaysia. BNPL integrations through HitPay are documented to increase average order values by up to 30% in relevant retail categories — see BNPL fees in Malaysia for a fee comparison. HitPay vs Stripe Malaysia — which is better for a small Malaysian business? HitPay is the stronger choice for Malaysian SMEs that need local e-wallet coverage. Stripe supports FPX, GrabPay, and cards in Malaysia but does not natively support Touch ‘n Go, ShopeePay, Boost, Atome, or GrabPay PayLater. HitPay supports all of these with no monthly fee and T+2 calendar day MYR payouts — compared to Stripe’s usage-based model that requires additional configuration for local methods. A full breakdown is available at HitPay vs Stripe Malaysia . Do I need a physical terminal to accept online payments in Malaysia? No. Online payment acceptance in Malaysia requires only a payment gateway account and an integration point — a website, online store, or payment link. Physical terminals are only needed for in-person transactions. HitPay supports both online and in-person acceptance through the same account.

title: The Patient You Lost Before They Ever Walked in the Door
summary: While the headlines at TCT and ACC focus on AI that can read angiograms or predict arrhythmias, a quieter, unsexy revolution is happening in the back office.
body_text: While the headlines at TCT and ACC focus on AI that can read angiograms or predict arrhythmias, a quieter, unsexy revolution is happening in the back office, and it might be the key to actually using those advanced clinical tools. The biggest bottleneck in modern cardiology is administrative friction.
