title: 6 Best Privacy.com Alternatives for Secure Virtual Payments in 2026
summary: Compare the top privacy.com alternatives for virtual cards and secure payments. Features, fees, and availability compared to help you choose.
body_text: Online payment fraud is getting harder to ignore. U.S. data breaches reached a record high in 2025, with 3,322 reported incidents, representing a 4% increase over the previous year. For everyday consumers, that translates to one very practical question: is your real card number floating around in a merchant database somewhere, just waiting to be stolen? Virtual cards were built to answer that question. Privacy.com popularized the concept, but its US-only availability, strict card limits on the free plan, and minimal budgeting integration push many users to look elsewhere. 42% of U.S . consumers used a virtual card in the past six months, and 65% say they're likely to use one in the next year, so the demand for strong alternatives has never been higher. If you're one of those consumers, this guide covers the six best Privacy.com alternatives in 2026, ranked by overall usefulness for the general user. Key Takeaways Privacy.com has real limitations: The free tier caps you at 12 cards per month, and single-use card numbers are not included. If you need more volume or richer controls, you need an alternative. Virtual cards are going mainstream: Virtual card adoption is particularly strong among tech-savvy millennials and Gen Z, who value the privacy and security benefits of virtual cards for online transactions. Act accordingly and protect yourself now. Budgeting-integrated cards beat standalone privacy cards: Tools like Envelope connect virtual card spending directly to your budget categories, offering protection and financial clarity in a single tool. International users must look beyond Privacy.com: Privacy.com's top complaints center on its US-only availability, requirement for a Social Security number, and lack of international access, meaning global users need alternatives built for their market. Fraud is the real driver: The FTC reported that more than 2.3 million consumers in the U.S. experienced fraud in 2022, equating to nearly $9 billion in losses. A virtual card is one of the most effective shields you can add to your digital financial life. Quick-Start Prioritization Framework Tool Best For Effort to Set Up Key Strength Envelope Budget-conscious households Low Virtual cards tied directly to spending envelopes Revolut International shoppers and travelers Low Disposable cards, multi-currency wallets Wise Global spending, 40+ currencies Low Mid-market exchange rates, no hidden fees Capital One Eno Existing Capital One cardholders Very Low Free, merchant-specific virtual numbers IronVest Privacy maximalists Medium Masked emails + phone + cards in one tool American Express Existing Amex business cardholders Low Integrated rewards, no separate account needed Start here based on your situation: You want virtual cards AND a budget system: Envelope, fastest path to both payment privacy and household spending control. You travel or shop internationally: Revolut or Wise, both handle multi-currency spending far better than Privacy.com. You already have a Capital One card: Eno is free, instant, and requires nothing extra to sign up for. You want full identity masking, not just card masking: IronVest bundles virtual cards with masked emails and phone numbers. 1. Envelope, Editor's Pick and Best for Budget-Connected Virtual Cards Most virtual card tools hand you a digital card number and call it done. Envelope takes a fundamentally different approach: it connects each virtual card directly to a spending envelope in your budget, so your payment protection and your financial planning live in the same place. How Envelope Works Envelope is a budgeting app with built-in checking and debit cards. It helps you organize money into digital envelopes, control spending before it happens, and manage household finances with more clarity. Envelope also lets you create virtual debit cards tied to specific envelopes. The practical impact of that design is significant. For example, you could create a "Netflix" virtual debit card that only has $20/month available. If the envelope does not have enough money, the card does not have extra money to pull from. You can also close the card anytime. This makes Envelope different from a simple privacy card tool. It is not only protecting your card number; it is connecting the card to your actual budget. That distinction matters for anyone who has ever been surprised by an auto-renewal charge or tried to cancel a subscription only to find the merchant keeps billing anyway. Pro Tip: Use one Envelope virtual card per subscription service. Set the envelope's monthly cap to the exact subscription price. If the merchant ever tries to charge more, a price hike, a surprise fee, or an unauthorized renewal, the card simply declines. You stay in control without lifting a finger. Pros: Virtual debit cards tied directly to individual budget envelopes Built-in checking account, so no separate bank account needed Envelope-level spending caps prevent overcharges and unwanted renewals Early paycheck access: get paid up to two days early with Envelope's early paycheck feature Real-time transaction notifications keep you aware of every charge Clean, modern interface designed for household budgeting Cons: Primarily US-focused, so international currency support is limited Requires opening a checking account, which involves identity verification Fewer standalone privacy masking features (email aliases, phone masks) compared to IronVest Best for: Individuals and households who want virtual card protection with real budgeting power baked in. 2. Revolut, Best for International Shoppers and Travelers Revolut has grown into one of the most versatile fintech platforms globally, and its virtual card capabilities make it a strong Privacy.com alternative for anyone who spends across borders. What Sets Revolut Apart One of Revolut's biggest advantages is its disposable virtual card technology. After each online transaction, the card details automatically change, reducing the risk of fraud and unauthorized purchases. This feature is particularly valuable for online shoppers who frequently buy from unfamiliar websites or international merchants. The app includes two-factor authentication, biometric login, instant card freeze, and transaction notifications. You can also create disposable virtual cards for safer online shopping on Premium and Metal plans. On pricing, Premium costs $9.99 per month and includes travel insurance, higher exchange limits, and priority support. Metal costs $16.99 per month and adds the highest savings APY and a stainless steel card. The Standard (free) plan includes a basic virtual card but without the auto-rotating disposable number feature. Pro Tip: If you sign up for free trials on websites you don't fully trust, use Revolut's disposable virtual card on Premium. The card number changes after the trial, making it impossible for the merchant to charge you again, even if they've stored your details. Pros: Disposable virtual card numbers that auto-rotate after each transaction (Premium/Metal) Multi-currency wallets with real interbank exchange rates Strong fraud monitoring with instant in-app card freezing Budgeting tools and expense tracking built into the same app Cons: Disposable virtual cards require a paid plan ($9.99/month) The main risk factor is the occasional account freeze that some users report during large or unusual transactions Revolut is not yet a fully licensed U.S. bank; it operates as an e-money institution and relies on banking partners for deposit services Best for: Frequent international shoppers or travelers who want a single app for spending, currency exchange, and virtual card security. 3. Wise, Best for Multi-Currency Virtual Spending Wise (formerly TransferWise) built its reputation on transparent international transfers, and its virtual card extends that philosophy to everyday spending across 40+ currencies. How the Wise Virtual Card Works The Wise Virtual Card is designed to offer convenience and security. Users can hold over 40 currencies at once, converting them in real-time using the mid-market exchange rate, a feature that minimizes hidden fees. You can have up to 3 virtual cards at any one time, which can make it easier to manage your budget by assigning different spending types to different cards. Wise virtual cards have different card details to your physical card, and can be frozen instantly whenever you're not using them, offering a handy added layer of security. Banks and traditional travel cards typically apply a spread; they buy currency at the mid-market rate and sell it to you at a worse rate, pocketing the difference. That difference is usually 2-5% and it's invisible because it's baked into the rate, not listed as a fee. Wise does not do this. That alone can save meaningful money for anyone who shops internationally. Pros: Mid-market exchange rates with no markup on supported currencies Up to 3 virtual cards included, free to create Works across 160+ countries with no foreign transaction fees when paying in a held currency Strong regulatory backing and transparent fee structure Cons: Requires full KYC identity verification Limited to 3 virtual cards at a time (far fewer than Privacy.com's 12/month free tier) Does not support cryptocurrency and has standard card features Best for: International users who want real exchange rates and a reliable virtual card for cross-border shopping. 4. Capital One Eno, Best Free Option for Existing Capital One Cardholders If you already carry a Capital One credit card, Eno is the simplest and fastest Privacy.com alternative available, and it costs nothing extra. How Eno Works Eno generates unique virtual card numbers for each website, protecting your actual credit card details during checkout. This feature lets you shop confidently without exposing your real credit card number. With Eno, you can easily lock or unlock virtual card numbers anytime, preventing unwanted charges and giving you full control over your online spending. Even if you get a new credit card, your virtual card numbers remain active and automatically update behind the scenes. The rewards angle is an important differentiator: all purchases made using these virtual numbers link directly to your Capital One account, so you continue to earn rewards and benefits seamlessly. Privacy.com's debit-based virtual cards earn nothing. With Eno, you keep your rewards while adding a security layer. Pros: Completely free for eligible Capital One cardholders Merchant-specific virtual numbers for strong fraud protection Rewards accumulate on the underlying credit card account The Eno browser extension is available for Chrome, Firefox, and Microsoft Edge Cons: Some Capital One cards are not eligible One have access to Capital One Eno It does not work in Safari, if you use Safari on a Mac, iPhone, or iPad, the Eno extension will not function Only available to existing Capital One customers, not a standalone product Best for: Capital One cardholders who want instant, free virtual card protection without signing up for a separate service. 5. IronVest, Best for Full Identity Masking Beyond Just Cards For users who want to go further than card-number protection, IronVest (formerly Blur by Abine) offers the most comprehensive privacy toolkit on this list. What IronVest Covers IronVest focuses heavily on online privacy and identity protection. While many virtual card providers emphasize business spending or international payments, IronVest's primary goal is helping users protect sensitive financial information during online transactions. The platform enables users to create virtual card numbers that shield real payment details from merchants. This reduces the risk of data breaches, unauthorized transactions, and identity theft. But it goes beyond payments. IronVest is a password manager platform that creates and manages user passwords on different websites. It offers masked email addresses, private phone numbers, and masked single-use debit cards. It's decentralized and offers 2FA authentication. On pricing: the free version of IronVest allows you to test two virtual cards, which they call "masked cards," after which you'll have to upgrade to their Plus ($6/mo) or Ultimate ($15/mo) plans for more. Pro Tip: Use IronVest's masked email feature alongside its virtual cards. Every website gets a unique forwarding address. If that address starts receiving spam, you know exactly which site sold your data, and you can kill that alias instantly, while your real inbox stays clean. Pros: Masked cards, masked emails, and masked phone numbers in one app The IronVest virtual payment solution does not require KYC and it can be funded with a credit card. The zero-knowledge architecture and distributed biometric security make phishing and identity theft extremely difficult Decentralized infrastructure means there is no single data source to breach Password manager functionality included Cons: You purchase the card using your own credit card ($2 fee) or your bank account, and top it up to make purchases, this prepaid model is less fluid than a linked debit setup Masked cards are actually pre-paid debit cards, not virtual credit cards, and there is a $2 fee per card created More complex to set up than simpler tools like Eno or Revolut Best for: Privacy-conscious individuals who want to mask their entire online identity, not just their card number. 6. American Express Virtual Cards, Best for Existing Amex Cardholders American Express has expanded its virtual card capabilities, making it a reasonable option for cardholders who want to add a layer of security without switching tools. How Amex Virtual Cards Work A virtual card number from American Express is a temporary, digital card credential that mirrors your existing Amex account for secure online and in-app purchases. You'll use it like your physical card, but the number, expiration, and security code are tokenized to reduce exposure. This setup strengthens online payment safety by isolating merchants from your actual card details. Core virtual card benefits include minimized fraud risk, controlled spending through per-merchant use, and simplified dispute handling. You maintain full rewards and protections, while limiting data reuse and enhancing checkout assurance. There is no fee to generate American Express virtual cards. However, access depends on having an eligible, active Amex account in good standing. Pros: No additional cost for eligible cardholders Full rewards and protections apply through your existing Amex account No new account, no KYC process, and no additional linked bank account required Tokenized numbers reduce merchant data exposure Cons: Only Citi and Capital One offer a complete virtual credit card solution for personal cards, American Express, Chase, and Discover offer similar but not identical solutions Limited to existing eligible Amex cardholders, not a standalone product Fewer spending controls (no per-envelope spending caps, no merchant-locking equivalent to Privacy.com) Best for: Existing American Express cardholders who want free, simple virtual card generation without adding a separate tool. Common Mistakes to Avoid When Choosing a Virtual Card Tool Ignoring the Card Limit Fine Print Privacy.com's free tier caps you at 12 cards per month. Many competing tools also impose limits. Before committing, count how many subscriptions and recurring charges you manage. If it's more than a dozen, you need a plan, or a tool, that can scale with you. Picking a Card Tool Without Budgeting Integration A virtual card protects your card number. A tool like Envelope protects your card number AND enforces your spending limits at the envelope level. If you only solve the privacy problem but not the overspending problem, you've only done half the job. Assuming Every Tool Works Internationally Privacy.com's top complaints include its US-only availability and lack of international access. The same limitation exists for several other tools. If you shop from international merchants or hold accounts in multiple currencies, Wise and Revolut are the two options built for that use case. Pro Tip: Before signing up for any virtual card tool, run through your last three months of online transactions. Note which merchants are international, which are subscription-based, and whether you've ever had an unauthorized charge. That audit tells you exactly which features you need, don't pay for tools that don't match your actual spending patterns. Frequently Asked Questions What is a virtual card and how does it protect me? A virtual card is a digital payment card with its own unique number, expiration date, and CVV that you use in place of your real card number when shopping online. A virtual card is a digital payment card that generates a unique card number, expiration date, and security code for online transactions. It functions like a regular debit or credit card but exists only in digital form. Virtual cards help protect your actual banking information and reduce the risk of fraud during online purchases. Is Privacy.com available outside the United States? No. Privacy.com's top complaints are its US-only availability, requirement for a Social Security number, and no support for international access. If you are outside the US, Wise and Revolut are the strongest alternatives to evaluate, as both support dozens of countries and multiple currencies. Can I still earn credit card rewards when using a virtual card? It depends on the tool. If you use a standalone tool like Privacy.com or IronVest, those are debit-based and carry no rewards. If you use a card-issuer's own virtual feature, like Capital One Eno or Amex's virtual card tool, all purchases made using those virtual numbers link directly to your credit card account, so you continue to earn rewards and benefits seamlessly. What makes Envelope different from other Privacy.com alternatives? Most virtual card tools stop at card-number masking. Envelope is different from a simple privacy card tool. It is not only protecting your card number; it is connecting the card to your actual budget. Each virtual card is tied to a spending envelope, so a subscription card for Netflix literally cannot charge you more than your Netflix envelope contains. That combination of protection and proactive budgeting is unique among consumer-facing tools. How many virtual cards do I actually need? In my experience, most households need one virtual card per active subscription, plus one or two general-purpose "burner" cards for one-off purchases from unfamiliar merchants. That typically works out to somewhere between 5 and 20 cards. Virtual cards are generally considered safer for online transactions, and many providers offer features such as disposable card numbers, spending limits, merchant-specific cards, and instant card freezing, so the right number depends on how many merchants you want to isolate from each other. title: PMB UHAMKA 2026: Jalur Masuk, Program Studi, dan Biaya Kuliah
summary: Simak informasi PMB UHAMKA 2026, mulai dari jalur prestasi, tes, rapor, nilai TKA, program studi, biaya pendaftaran, hingga simulasi cicilan Danacita.
body_text: Daftar isi PMB Universitas Muhammadiyah Prof. Dr. HAMKA (UHAMKA) 2026 Jalur Masuk, Fakultas, Program Studi, Biaya Kuliah, dan Cara Daftar Universitas Muhammadiyah Prof. Dr. HAMKA (UHAMKA) merupakan perguruan tinggi Muhammadiyah di Jakarta yang menyediakan berbagai pilihan program pendidikan, mulai dari Diploma, Sarjana, Profesi, Magister, hingga Doktor. Portal PMB UHAMKA saat ini mencantumkan 48 program studi dan 12 fakultas. Untuk calon mahasiswa, UHAMKA menyediakan beberapa jalur penerimaan yang dapat dipilih sesuai prestasi, nilai akademik, atau hasil tes. Profil UHAMKA UHAMKA merupakan perguruan tinggi yang mengintegrasikan pendidikan dengan nilai-nilai Islam dan Muhammadiyah. Pilihan program studinya mencakup bidang pendidikan, ekonomi dan bisnis, teknologi, kesehatan, komunikasi, psikologi, hukum, serta bidang keislaman. UHAMKA juga menyediakan beberapa pilihan jenjang pendidikan, termasuk program reguler, kelas karyawan, RPL, profesi, magister, dan doktor. Visi UHAMKA UHAMKA memiliki visi untuk menjadi perguruan tinggi utama dalam mencerdaskan kehidupan bangsa melalui pendidikan, penelitian, dan pengabdian kepada masyarakat yang berlandaskan nilai-nilai Islam. Misi UHAMKA UHAMKA menjalankan misi melalui: Penyelenggaraan pendidikan yang berkualitas dan berlandaskan nilai Islam. Pengembangan penelitian dan inovasi untuk menjawab kebutuhan masyarakat. Pelaksanaan pengabdian kepada masyarakat secara berkelanjutan. Pengembangan sumber daya manusia yang unggul, berakhlak, dan berdaya saing. Keunggulan UHAMKA Pilihan program studi beragam, dari pendidikan, bisnis, teknologi, kesehatan, hingga komunikasi. Berbasis nilai Islam, dengan pengembangan akademik yang terintegrasi dengan nilai Muhammadiyah. Pilihan jenjang lengkap, mulai dari Diploma hingga Doktor. Berbagai jalur masuk, termasuk Prestasi, Tes, Undangan, Rapor, Nilai TKA, dan RPL. Fakultas dan Program Studi UHAMKA UHAMKA memiliki berbagai fakultas dengan pilihan program studi yang cukup beragam. Fakultas Keguruan dan Ilmu Pendidikan Berfokus pada bidang pendidikan dan keguruan. Program Studi: Bimbingan dan Konseling PGSD PGPAUD Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris Pendidikan Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia Pendidikan Matematika Pendidikan Biologi Pendidikan Fisika Pendidikan Ekonomi Pendidikan Sejarah Pendidikan Geografi Pendidikan Bahasa Jepang Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Menyediakan program di bidang ekonomi, bisnis, dan manajemen. Program Studi: Akuntansi Manajemen Ekonomi Islam Perpajakan Fakultas Farmasi dan Sains Berfokus pada bidang farmasi dan kesehatan laboratorium. Program Studi: Farmasi Analisis Kesehatan Profesi Apoteker Fakultas Teknologi Industri dan Informatika Menyediakan program studi di bidang teknologi dan teknik. Program Studi: Teknik Informatika Sistem dan Teknologi Informasi Teknik Elektro Teknik Mesin Teknik Rekayasa Mekatronika Fakultas Ilmu Sosial dan Ilmu Politik Berfokus pada bidang komunikasi dan ilmu sosial. Program Studi: Ilmu Komunikasi Produksi Media Fakultas Ilmu Kesehatan Menyediakan program di bidang kesehatan masyarakat dan gizi. Program Studi: Kesehatan Masyarakat Gizi Fakultas Psikologi Program Studi: Psikologi Fakultas Agama Islam Menyediakan program studi yang berkaitan dengan pendidikan dan ekonomi syariah. Program Studi: Pendidikan Agama Islam Pendidikan Bahasa Arab Perbankan Syariah Fakultas Hukum Program Studi: Hukum Bisnis Fakultas Kedokteran Program Studi: Pendidikan Dokter Profesi Dokter Teknik Kardiovaskuler UHAMKA juga memiliki Sekolah Pascasarjana yang menyediakan berbagai program Magister dan Doktor. PMB UHAMKA 2026 UHAMKA menyediakan beberapa jalur penerimaan mahasiswa baru. Portal PMB mencantumkan Jalur Prestasi, Tes, SBMPTMU, RPL, Nilai TKA, dan Rapor. Jalur Masuk UHAMKA 2026 1. Jalur Prestasi Jalur ini menggunakan prestasi calon mahasiswa sebagai dasar seleksi. Peserta dapat memilih maksimal dua program studi, kecuali Kedokteran. Biaya pendaftaran sebesar Rp250.000. 2. Jalur Tes Seleksi dilakukan melalui ujian berbasis komputer atau CBT. Materi tes meliputi TPA dan Bahasa Inggris. Peserta dapat memilih maksimal dua program studi, kecuali Kedokteran. Jalur Rapor Seleksi dilakukan berdasarkan nilai rapor dua semester terakhir. Peserta dapat memilih maksimal dua program studi, kecuali Kedokteran. Jalur Nilai TKA Seleksi menggunakan hasil Tes Kemampuan Akademik (TKA) dan nilai rapor dua semester terakhir. Peserta dapat memilih maksimal dua program studi, kecuali Kedokteran. 5. Jalur Undangan Jalur ini ditujukan bagi siswa SMA/SMK/MA yang memperoleh undangan dan dapat mendaftar tanpa mengikuti tes. Peserta dapat memilih satu program studi, kecuali Kedokteran. 6. Jalur RPL Jalur Rekognisi Pembelajaran Lampau ditujukan bagi calon mahasiswa yang memiliki pengalaman atau pembelajaran sebelumnya yang dapat diakui untuk melanjutkan pendidikan. Portal pendaftaran UHAMKA menyediakan jalur RPL sebagai pilihan tersendiri. Persyaratan Pendaftaran UHAMKA Persyaratan dapat berbeda berdasarkan jalur dan program studi. Untuk program reguler, sebagian besar prodi mensyaratkan lulusan SMA/SMK/MA. Program tertentu memiliki persyaratan khusus, seperti SMA IPA untuk Kedokteran dan beberapa program kesehatan. Cara Daftar PMB UHAMKA 2026 Pendaftaran dilakukan secara online melalui portal PMB UHAMKA dengan tahapan: Membuat akun pendaftaran. Memilih jalur dan program studi. Mengisi data pendaftaran. Mengunggah dokumen yang diperlukan. Membayar biaya pendaftaran. Mengikuti proses seleksi sesuai jalur. Melakukan daftar ulang jika dinyatakan diterima. Jadwal PMB UHAMKA 2026 Beberapa jalur PMB UHAMKA seperti Prestasi, Tes, Rapor, dan Nilai TKA dibuka sepanjang periode pendaftaran dan dapat dilakukan setiap hari sesuai ketentuan masing-masing jalur. Hasil seleksi untuk beberapa jalur diumumkan maksimal 7 hari kerja setelah dokumen diunggah. Untuk informasi tanggal gelombang terbaru, calon mahasiswa disarankan mengecek portal PMB UHAMKA sebelum melakukan pendaftaran. Biaya Pendaftaran UHAMKA 2026 Untuk sebagian besar program reguler, biaya formulir pendaftaran adalah Rp250.000. Biaya pra-kuliah sebesar Rp500.000, sedangkan her registrasi sebesar Rp100.000 dan dibayarkan setiap awal semester gasal. Untuk program tertentu, biaya formulir dapat berbeda. Misalnya, Profesi Apoteker dan Profesi Dokter memiliki ketentuan khusus. Biaya Kuliah UHAMKA 2026/2027 Portal PMB UHAMKA menyediakan informasi biaya kuliah berdasarkan program studi dan jenjang. Namun, pada halaman biaya resmi yang dapat diverifikasi saat ini, nominal biaya per semester untuk sebagian besar program S1 tidak tampil pada tabel teks. Karena itu, angka tersebut tidak dicantumkan agar tidak menggunakan nominal yang tidak terverifikasi. Program / Bidang Semester 1–4 Semester 5–Lulus Bimbingan dan Konseling Rp8.300.000 Rp6.500.000 S1 Gizi Rp11.400.000 Rp8.900.000 Ekonomi & Bisnis / Sosial Rp8.000.000–Rp11.000.000 — S1 Pendidikan Dokter Mulai sekitar Rp19.000.000 — Kuliah di UHAMKA dengan Cicilan Danacita Danacita dapat menjadi alternatif pembiayaan pendidikan untuk membantu mahasiswa mengatur pembayaran biaya kuliah secara bertahap sesuai tenor dan hasil evaluasi pengajuan. Simulasi Cicilan Biaya Kuliah UHAMKA Bersama Danacita Karena nominal biaya semester untuk lima program S1 pilihan belum tercantum secara terbaca pada sumber resmi yang tersedia, simulasi cicilan Danacita untuk kelima prodi belum dapat dihitung secara akurat. Sebagai contoh, biaya yang memang dipublikasikan UHAMKA dapat dihitung sebagai berikut: Program / Bidang Biaya yang Disimulasikan 3 Bulan 6 Bulan 12 Bulan Bimbingan dan Konseling Rp8.300.000 Rp2.766.667 Rp1.383.333 Rp691.667 S1 Gizi Rp11.400.000 Rp3.800.000 Rp1.900.000 Rp950.000 Ekonomi & Bisnis / Sosial Rp8.000.000–Rp11.000.000 Rp2.666.667–Rp3.666.667 Rp1.333.333–Rp1.833.333 Rp666.667–Rp916.667 S1 Pendidikan Dokter Rp588.000.000* Rp196.000.000 Rp98.000.000 Rp49.000.000 *Untuk Pendidikan Dokter, Rp588 juta merupakan perkiraan total biaya hingga lulus , sehingga simulasi di atas hanya ilustrasi pembagian total biaya dan bukan cicilan per semester . Catatan: Simulasi ini hanya untuk memberikan gambaran nominal pembagian biaya. Bukan tagihan resmi UHAMKA maupun keputusan pembiayaan final Danacita. Nominal aktual dapat berbeda sesuai biaya yang dibiayai, tenor, biaya layanan, dan hasil persetujuan pengajuan. Catatan untuk Calon Mahasiswa Cek jalur dan persyaratan sesuai program studi yang dipilih. Biaya pendaftaran dan kuliah dapat berbeda berdasarkan program. Beberapa program memiliki persyaratan khusus. Simulasi Danacita bersifat ilustratif dan bukan keputusan pembiayaan final.

title: Safe Pro Reports Record 1,336% Revenue Growth in Q2 2026 Driven by Multiple Government Contracts for AI-Powered Threat Detection and Mapping
summary: AVENTURA, Fla., Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Safe Pro Group Inc. (Nasdaq: SPAI) ("Safe Pro" or the "Company"), a developer of artificial intelligence
body_text: Safe Pro’s AI Gross Margins hit 75% for Second Quarter as Interest in its Patented AI-Powered Computer Vision Technologies for Aerial and Ground-Based Military Applications Grows AVENTURA, Fla., Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Safe Pro Group Inc. (Nasdaq: SPAI) (“Safe Pro” or the “Company”), a developer of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled defense, security, and situational awareness solutions, today announced financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 highlighted by record AI revenue, expanding AI gross margins, and continued U.S. government contract momentum. Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights Include: Continued Record Revenue Growth and High Margins Driven by AI Product Sales The Company’s quarterly revenue of $1,332,074 represents a 1,336% increase from $92,753 reported in the second quarter of 2025. Quarterly sales in the Company’s AI subsidiary surged over 3,084%, as compared to the same quarter of 2025, driven by new U.S. Army-contracted sales of its AI-powered, edge compute Navigation, Observation & Detection Engine (NODE) and services and support revenue. Safe Pro’s AI gross margin of 75% for the second quarter underscores the scalability and profitability of the Company’s software and edge compute product lines. During the second quarter of 2026, the Company completed its Board-approved common stock repurchase program, having purchased a total of 637,084 shares in the open market during the program, of which, 474,630 shares were purchased during the six months ended June 30, 2026. Demand for Real Time Battlefield Situational Awareness Drives AI-Powered Threat Detection & Mapping Subcontracts Safe Pro received four government contracts in Q2 highlighted by its NODE edge-based threat detection and mapping solution and services in support of the U.S. Army and a Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) award from the U.S. Air Force for AI dataset development for use in airfield operations. Company Expands Market Potential with Enhanced Capabilities for Autonomous Ground and Aerial Vehicles Safe Pro AI received an award from a leading U.S. defense prime contractor, to integrate its real-time AI-powered explosive threat detection technology onboard next-generation autonomous Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) for on-the-move battlefield operations. The Company successfully advanced its technology development efforts demonstrating the integration of its new InFlight, embeddable, real-time AI-powered threat detection package. InFlight AI can natively process real-time video onboard a drone at the tactical edge, delivering live threat data directly into mission planning ecosystems such as the U.S. Army’s Tactical Assault Kit (ATAK), enhancing and accelerating decision making critical to mission success. “The increasing number of contract awards Safe Pro has received this year for our patented AI-powered threat detection and mapping technology validates what we believe is a large and urgent unmet need for real-time, ground-truth situational awareness across the defense sector,” said Dan Erdberg, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Safe Pro Group Inc. “Our investments through the first half of 2026 in personnel, technology development, inventory, and disciplined capital allocation including our completed share repurchase program, are aligned with what we believe is a growing, high-margin, government contract revenue base. We believe the underlying fundamentals position Safe Pro for sustained long-term growth as adoption of our unique edge compute threat detection technology accelerates across aerial and ground-based military platforms.” As previously announced, Safe Pro will be hosting an Innovation Day on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, in Aventura, Florida. The event, which features live drone operations highlighting how American AI is utilized in the field, is scheduled to begin at approximately 8:30 a.m. ET and conclude by 12:30 p.m. ET. Supporting materials will be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on August 25, 2026. The Company’s Safe Pro Object Threat Detection (SPOTD) AI platform analyzes imagery and video from virtually any drone to automatically detect and classify explosive threats and other objects of interest. The platform converts raw video into high-resolution 2D/3D geospatial models that can be rapidly shared to support operational decision-making in defense, security, and humanitarian missions. SPOTD can identify more than 150 types of landmines and UXO , enabling scalable situational awareness across large, high-risk areas. SPOTD has been deployed in active operational environments in Ukraine for nearly three years and is supported by a growing proprietary dataset comprising over 2.9 million analyzed images , more than 54,328 identified threats , and coverage of approximately 37,900 acres . The financial information included in this press release should be read in conjunction with the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission today. For more information about Safe Pro’s real-world landmine and UXO detections, visit: https://safeproai.com/landmine-detections/ . For information about Safe Pro Group, its subsidiaries, and technologies, please visit https://safeprogroup.com and connect with us on LinkedIn , Facebook , and X . A bout Safe Pro Group Inc. Safe Pro Group Inc. (Nasdaq: SPAI) is a mission-driven technology company delivering AI-enabled security and defense solutions. Through cutting-edge platforms like SPOTD, Safe Pro provides advanced situational awareness tools for defense, humanitarian, and homeland security applications globally. The Company is a leading provider of artificial intelligence (AI) solutions specializing in drone imagery processing, leveraging commercially available off-the-shelf drones with its proprietary machine learning and computer vision technology to enable rapid identification of explosive threats, providing a safer and more efficient alternative to traditional human-based analysis methods. title: How Wholesale Distributors Automate Invoicing Across ERP, CRM, and Complex Pricing

body_text: Key Takeaways Data silos cause billing errors, slow collections, and unreliable forecasts that undermine wholesale invoicing accuracy. CRM-to-ERP integration suits subscription and recurring-revenue distributors, cutting days sales outstanding by 5 to 15 days. ERP systems with billing modules deliver strong pricing flexibility and roughly 35% faster order management, though setup effort runs high. Automated invoicing pays off fastest in improved cash flow rather than reduced headcount for subscription-based wholesale distributors. Most distributors run a combination of systems. Pairing an ERP with a B2B platform typically beats a single all-in-one suite. AR automation layers offer low setup effort and same-day billing, making them ideal for fast cash application. Standalone accounting with manual entry keeps labor costs high and suits only distributors with tiny order volumes. Quick Summary Automating wholesale invoicing means connecting your ERP, CRM, and pricing rules so an order becomes an accurate invoice without anyone rekeying data. For subscription-based distributors juggling recurring shipments and dynamic pricing, that connection is where the real money hides. The payoff shows up fastest in cash flow, not headcount. Consolidate order and customer data into one source. Wire pricing logic into the invoice trigger. Let recurring billing fire on its own. That’s the most direct path to automation. Eliminating data silos prevents billing errors, slow collections, and unreliable forecasts. What Should You Compare Before You Start? Not every tool fits every distributor. The best wholesale software differs from business to business because features are specialized, so match the tool type to your actual channels. Below is how the common approaches stack up on the metrics that matter. Approach Setup effort Difficulty Pricing flexibility Best for ROI signal Standalone accounting + manual entry Low Easy Weak Tiny order volume Minimal; labor stays high ERP with billing module High Hard Strong Full operational control 35% faster order management B2B commerce platform Medium Moderate Moderate Digital wholesale channels Faster order sync CRM-to-ERP integration Medium Moderate Strong Subscription + recurring revenue 5-15 day DSO reduction AR automation layer Low Easy Strong Fast cash application Same-day billing Many distributors run a combination rather than one system. Integrating an ERP with a B2B platform is common, and it usually beats forcing everything into a single suite. How Long Does It Take and What’s the Payoff? Expect a phased rollout, not a weekend project. A CRM-to-ERP integration for order-to-cash typically lands in the moderate-difficulty range. Simple AR automation layers land faster because they sit on top of what you already run. The financial case is concrete. U.S. Wholesale distribution is an $8.2 trillion industry , and 43% of credit-based B2B sales run overdue on average terms of 46 days. That’s a structural collection problem, and faster automated invoicing is a direct lever against it. The ROI concentrates in cash timing. Same-day or next-day billing paired with significant acceleration in collections attacks that 46-day drag more than any labor saving does. You get paid sooner, and the money you’re already owed stops aging. Why Does Data Visibility Drive the Numbers? Consolidated data is what makes accurate billing and reliable forecasting possible at the same time. Your matching engine, your pricing accuracy, and your collections speed all depend on killing the silos first. Automate the plumbing, and the invoicing takes care of itself. Identifying Invoicing Pain Points and Data Silos Manual wholesale invoicing usually breaks in the handoff between systems. An order lives in your CRM, pricing sits in a spreadsheet, and someone in accounting rekeys it all into the ERP to cut an invoice. That gap is where the errors, delays, and disputes originate. Automating wholesale invoicing starts with finding those gaps, not buying software. For subscription-based distributors, the pain compounds. You bill the same customer on a recurring cycle, often with contract-specific rates that changed last quarter. When systems don’t communicate, every renewal presents a chance to invoice the wrong price or miss a shipment entirely. Where Do the Data Silos Actually Live? A data silo holds information other systems cannot reach without manual intervention. In wholesale distribution, silos hide in three places: order data in the CRM, inventory and pricing in the ERP, and payment history in accounting. Each one is accurate on its own, but they fail to align automatically. A distribution guide from Anchor Group makes the point that generic accounting software operates in silos while a purpose-built wholesale ERP connects inventory, orders, pricing, and financials. That matters most as you scale. Most distributors hit the wall and need specialized systems somewhere between $5M and $20M in revenue, when manual reconciliation stops keeping up with volume. The silo tax shows up as slow cash. When a rep closes a deal in the CRM but billing can’t see it for two days, you add two days to every collection cycle before anyone even chases payment. How Do Data Silos Hurt Cash Flow and Customers? Silos attack cash flow directly. Codeless Platforms found that CRM-to-ERP integration accelerates the billing cycle, enabling same-day or next-day invoicing. The customer side is quieter but just as costly. An industrial packaging distributor with disconnected order-processing and customer-service systems couldn’t give straight answers on order status or billing. After consolidating into one source of truth , it got cleaner financial reporting and better service. Wrong invoices don’t just delay payment; they erode trust with the accounts you most want to keep on subscription. One healthcare distributor integrated its CRM, ERP, and internal databases to automate order processing, credit control, invoicing, and collections in a single flow. The result was fewer manual admin hours and stronger cash collection. The Real Fix: Integration Over Monoliths Single-platform vendors argue one unified system solves everything. Independent guides counter that fit to your operating model, your revenue band, warehouse complexity, and existing stack, matters more than consolidation. Both are partly right. Consolidation is the goal, but the path is integrating specialized tools, not forcing one monolith. Watch implementation carefully. Rollout costs typically run one to three times the annual software cost, so the risk sits in execution, not the license. A gap in your order-to-cash cycle survives a bad rollout no matter how good the tool is. Integrating ERP with CRM for Unified Customer Data Your ERP and CRM do two different jobs, and automated invoicing lives in the gap between them. The CRM owns the relationship: who the customer is, what contract they signed, which rates apply. The ERP owns the transaction: inventory, order fulfillment, financials, and the invoice itself. When they don’t share data, someone rekeys it by hand, and that’s exactly where recurring billing breaks. Connecting the two is the core of invoicing without adding staff. An integrated pipeline means an order captured in the CRM flows straight into the ERP, gets priced by your rules engine, and fires an invoice with no manual touch. For subscription distributors, that same pipeline handles the next cycle automatically. Why Integrate ERP and CRM at All? The payoff is fewer errors and less rework, not just cleaner records. Manual data entry between disconnected systems carries an error rate estimated at around 1% , and each bad invoice line triggers a dispute, a credit memo, and a delayed payment. At wholesale volumes, a fraction of a percent turns into hundreds of correction cycles a month. An integrated pipeline removes the rekeying step where those errors originate. This does more than speed up admin; it cuts the disputes that stall collection in the first place. Order accuracy compounds too, since a line priced correctly at capture never becomes a downstream argument with a customer. If your recurring revenue depends on renewals firing accurately, that clean handoff is the difference between a forecast you trust and one you guess at. What Are the Technical Requirements? An API-based integration provides a real-time connection that syncs customer, order, and pricing data between CRM and ERP the moment it changes. For higher-volume distributors, an integration layer (iPaaS) sits in the middle, managing workflows and reshaping data formats so mismatched fields line up. The pricing engine is where the real value concentrates. A rules engine handling customer-specific, quantity-break, date-sensitive, and multi-currency rates does two jobs at once. It prices every line correctly, and it generates an audit trail. Each invoice line becomes a traceable, rule-derived record instead of a manual entry. For regulated distributors in food or pharmaceutical goods that need lot tracking and compliance documentation, that trail is a strict requirement. How Do Distributors Make It Work in Practice? Focus first on high-impact workflows: order creation and invoice visibility. Automating the flow from CRM to ERP eliminates the lag between deal closure and invoice generation, which directly improves cash collection. A multi-location farm market operator tied CRM, ERP, and inventory together to reduce manual reconciliation across sites. Single-platform vendors sell one monolith as the answer. In practice, consolidation is the right goal, but the path is integrating specialized tools, not forcing everything into one box. A CRM built for wholesale beats a generic enterprise CRM that misses volume pricing and inventory-dependent selling. Because implementation represents a significant upfront investment, a sloppy integration can sink a good system. Phase the rollout to prove the quick wins first. For teams still stuck between systems, Blixo offers custom ERP integrations for platforms like Oracle, SAP, and Microsoft Dynamics, plus accounting connections to QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, and NetSuite, so the handoffs that leak time get automated instead. Automating Complex Pricing Rules in ERP Complex pricing is where most wholesale invoicing automation earns or loses its keep. Your ERP has to price the same SKU differently for a dozen customers, apply quantity breaks mid-order, honor contract rates that expired last week, and do it across currencies and tax regimes. Get the rules engine right and every invoice line derives from logic instead of memory. For subscription distributors, this is the heart of automating wholesale invoicing. Recurring shipments mean the pricing engine fires again and again without a human checking each cycle. The rules have to be airtight before you ever turn on automation. What Kinds of Pricing Rules Break Automation? The rules that trip up ERP pricing are the ones that stack. Customer-specific pricing, quantity-break tiers, and date-sensitive contract rates all have to resolve in the right order for a single line item. Modern distribution platforms like Dynamics 365 Business Central support all three natively, plus multiple currencies and tax regimes for distributors selling across borders. A customer might have a negotiated base rate, a volume discount that kicks in at 500 units, and a promotional price that overrides both until month-end. If your ERP resolves those in the wrong sequence, the invoice is wrong and nobody notices until the dispute lands. That’s why the rules engine matters more than the invoice template. In practice, complex pricing and compliance are the same problem seen from two sides. When every invoice line is a traceable, rule-derived record instead of a manual entry, you get the audit trail regulated distributors need anyway. Food distributors tracking lot and expiration data, or pharma distributors managing DEA serialization, get cleaner records as a byproduct of pricing automation. How Do You Automate Pricing Without Getting Burned? Validate and test the rules before you flip the switch, then run them in parallel against manual pricing until the numbers match. Effective distribution ERP implementations push order accuracy from the 96-97% range to over 99%. That gap represents disputes, returns, and support tickets you stop paying for. Build in data validation at the point of entry so bad customer or contract data can’t reach the pricing engine. Then test edge cases deliberately: expired contracts, overlapping promotions, minimum-order thresholds. A rule that works for 95% of orders and silently fails the rest is worse than no automation, because you trust it. There’s a real debate here. One camp says picking the right system is the key decision. The independent guides push back: implementation quality decides the outcome, and a bad rollout sinks even a great system. The real risk sits in how you configure and test the rules, not in the license you signed. Skip heavy pricing automation if your catalog is small and your rates rarely change. The setup effort only pays back when the pricing complexity is real and recurring. Real-Time Inventory Visibility for Accurate Billing Inventory that’s wrong on paper is inventory that bills wrong in practice. When your stock counts lag reality, you invoice for units you can’t ship, backorder items you already sold, or credit customers after the fact. For subscription distributors billing the same accounts every cycle, that error repeats until someone catches it. Real-time visibility is the fix, and it’s a core piece of wholesale invoicing without generating disputes. Real-time inventory visibility means your ERP, CRM, and warehouse systems share one live stock count, so an invoice only fires for what’s actually available to ship. That single source of truth is what turns automated billing from a liability into a cash engine. Distributors that move from periodic counts to live tracking commonly cut safety stock while raising fill rates, and warehouse studies tie barcode or RFID-driven counts to picking accuracy above 98%. Those last few points are the difference between clean invoices and a queue of credit memos. Why Do Inventory Errors Break Automated Billing? Automation amplifies whatever it’s fed. Feed it a stale stock count and it bills the wrong thing at machine speed. The damage lands on cash flow first: a single disputed invoice can sit unresolved for weeks, and research on B2B collections puts the cost of resolving one billing error at roughly $50 to $100 in staff time before the payment even clears. Accurate inventory is the precondition for fast billing working at all. Bill fast on bad data and you just accelerate the dispute, adding a credit memo and a re-invoice to every shortcut you thought you were taking. For regulated distributors, the stakes climb. Food and pharmaceutical operations need lot tracking, expiration management, and serialization tied to every line. When inventory visibility feeds the invoice directly, each billed unit carries its own traceable record instead of a manual note someone typed in after picking. How Do Matching Engines Keep Invoices Accurate? A matching engine reconciles the order, the shipment, and the invoice automatically, flagging mismatches before a bill goes out. It compares what was ordered in the CRM against what shipped from the warehouse against what the pricing rules say, then either clears the invoice or holds it for review. The technical requirement is real-time synchronization through API-based integration or an EDI layer that automates the transfer of orders and invoices. One B2B platform reports 120+ ERP integrations for automated order sync, which shows the direction the market is moving: distributors run multiple systems and stitch them together rather than buying one monolith. Stitching these systems together ensures that order sync happens automatically, reducing manual admin hours. Similarly, linking inventory across multiple sites reduces the need for manual reconciliation. Selection or Execution: Where’s the Real Risk? Feature comparison eats most of buyers’ attention, but rollout execution decides the outcome. The industry splits here. One view says picking the right system is the key decision; another argues a poor implementation sinks even a strong platform. The best approach is to match the system to your channels and pricing complexity first, then spend your risk budget on a phased rollout and clean data migration. The license is cheap next to a botched go-live, especially since implementation costs can easily exceed the initial software investment. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Should I automate invoicing if my distributor only does 50 orders a month? Manual entry makes sense at tiny volumes because the setup effort outweighs the labor saved. However, as order volume grows and error correction costs rise, manual reconciliation quickly becomes unsustainable. 2. Can I run a B2B commerce platform and an ERP at the same time without doubling my work? Yes, and it’s common. Pairing an ERP with a B2B platform typically beats forcing everything into one suite because each handles what it’s built for. API-based integration syncs orders and inventory in real time, so you get specialized tools without manual handoffs between them. 3. What happens if my pricing rules overlap or conflict during automation? Your ERP resolves stacked rules in sequence, so the order matters. A customer with a negotiated rate, a volume discount, and a promotional price must have the engine apply them correctly or the invoice will be wrong. To prevent errors, map out your pricing hierarchy clearly and run test scenarios—such as overlapping discounts—to ensure the system resolves them in the correct order. 4. Why does real-time inventory visibility matter more for subscription distributors than one-time buyers? Subscription billing fires repeatedly without manual checks, meaning a single inventory error will recur on every cycle. While a one-time buyer’s stock issue is resolved quickly, recurring errors compound, leading to repeated disputes and administrative cleanup. 5. If I integrate CRM and ERP, will I still need people to review invoices before they go out? A matching engine can reconcile orders, shipments, and pricing automatically and flag mismatches for review, but edge cases and disputed terms still need human judgment. The goal is removing rekeying and routine errors, not eliminating oversight. High-impact workflows like order creation benefit most from automation. 6. How do I know if my rollout is going badly before it costs real money? Run automated pricing in parallel with manual pricing until the numbers align consistently. A successful rollout should show a measurable drop in billing disputes and credit memos right away. If disputes or credit memos increase after go-live, the implementation has a problem worth stopping to fix. 7. Does automating wholesale invoicing reduce headcount or just speed up cash? The payoff concentrates in faster cash flow rather than labor cuts. Accelerating the billing cycle targets the structural collection delays common in B2B credit sales. While reducing admin hours is helpful, the primary financial benefit is getting paid sooner and keeping capital moving.

title: Rocket Lab Corporation Announces Progress on Iridium Acquisition: HSR Period Lapses; Form S-4 Filed; FCC Applications Filed; Capital Strategy Underway
summary: LONG BEACH, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB) (“Rocket Lab” or the “Company”), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced substantial milestones in connection with its previously announced proposed acquisition of Iridium
body_text: Rocket Lab Corporation Announces Progress on Iridium Acquisition: HSR Period Lapses; Form S-4 Filed; FCC Applications Filed; Capital Strategy Underway August 13, 2026 PDF Version LONG BEACH, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB) (“Rocket Lab” or the “Company”), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced substantial milestones in connection with its previously announced proposed acquisition of Iridium Communications Inc. (“Iridium”). Regulatory Clearance and Filings Rocket Lab announced today that the waiting period under the U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (“HSR”), in connection with its pending acquisition of Iridium expired at 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time, on August 12, 2026. Rocket Lab also today filed its Registration Statement on Form S-4 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) related to the Iridium acquisition to register the Rocket Lab securities to be delivered to Iridium shareholders to satisfy the equity consideration at the closing of the transaction. The filing of the registration statement represents a substantial step in the process toward completing the proposed transaction. The registration statement has not yet become effective, and the securities described in it may not be sold, nor may offers to buy be accepted, prior to the time the registration statement becomes effective. Rocket Lab further announced that on August 10, 2026, Rocket Lab and Iridium filed with the Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) applications seeking its consent to transfer control of Iridium’s licenses and authorizations to Rocket Lab. Sir Peter Beck, founder and CEO of Rocket Lab, says: “Filing the Form S-4 and the FCC applications and receiving U.S. antitrust clearance are all major steps for us in the execution timeline for the Iridium acquisition. These milestones continue to pave the way toward the completion of this transformative transaction that will position Rocket Lab to accelerate our future into space applications.” Capital Strategy As previously reported, in connection with signing the definitive merger agreement to acquire Iridium, Rocket Lab entered into a commitment letter with Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., Wells Fargo Bank, National Association and Wells Fargo Securities, LLC and Deutsche Bank AG New York Branch for a 364-day senior secured bridge term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of $3.6 billion. The Company intends to replace the commitments for the bridge facility through a combination of permanent debt and equity financing sources. As part of its financing strategy, Rocket Lab announced today that, together with Iridium, it intends to seek certain amendments to Iridium’s existing term loan credit facility with an aggregate amount of $1.775 billion outstanding as of June 30, 2026, which would allow the Iridium facility to remain in place following Rocket Lab’s acquisition, and which would reduce the Company’s debt commitments correspondingly at much more attractive rates than the bridge facility terms. Such amendments, if completed, will require the consent of lenders under Iridium’s facility, and there is no assurance at this time that the Company will obtain such consents. The Company also separately announced today a new at the market program that replaces the Company’s May 2026 program and carries forward the unsold offering amount under that prior program. Amounts raised under the new program are intended to reduce the remaining commitments under the bridge loan through equity transactions. About Rocket Lab Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world’s most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab’s satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com . Additional Information and Where to Find It This communication is being made in respect of a proposed transaction involving Rocket Lab Corporation (“Rocket Lab”) and Iridium Communications Inc. (“Iridium”). In connection with the proposed transaction, Rocket Lab has filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a Registration Statement on Form S-4 that includes the proxy statement of Iridium that will also constitute a prospectus of Rocket Lab, but which is not yet effective. When the proxy statement/prospectus is finalized, it will be sent to the stockholders of Iridium seeking their approval of certain transaction-related proposals. title: Sicherheitsbestand berechnen: Formeln und Methoden, die zu Ihren Daten passen
summary: Erfahren Sie, wie Sie den Sicherheitsbestand mit der Durchschnitts-Max-Methode und anhand von Z-Score-Formeln berechnen, und sehen Sie sich ein Beispiel für drei verschiedene Servicelevels an.
body_text: In diesem Artikel erfahren Sie: • Wovor der Sicherheitsbestand schützt und worin er sich vom Umlaufbestand (Cycle Stock) und vom Meldebestand (Reorder Point) unterscheidet • Wie die Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode funktioniert, warum sie der schnellste Einstieg ist und wo sie zu hohe Puffer erzeugt • Wie die Z-Wert-Formel für Bedarfsschwankungen aufgebaut ist und wie Ihr Servicegrad die Puffergröße bestimmt Die meisten Werte für den Sicherheitsbestand beginnen als fundierte Schätzung. Eine Planerin oder ein Planer legt eine Reichweite von ein paar Wochen fest, rundet der Sicherheit halber auf und macht weiter. Das funktioniert so lange, bis ein Fehlbestand oder ein Audit die Frage aufwirft, woher diese Zahl eigentlich stammt. Der Sicherheitsbestand ist eine berechenbare Größe, die von drei Faktoren abhängt: • Wie stark Ihr Bedarf schwankt • Wie stark Ihre Wiederbeschaffungszeit schwankt • Welchen Servicegrad Sie sich leisten wollen Sie brauchen nicht immer die anspruchsvollste Formel, aber Sie brauchen eine, die zu Ihrer Datenlage passt. Dieser Leitfaden geht die Methoden von der einfachsten bis zur komplexesten durch, damit Sie den für Ihr Unternehmen richtigen Ansatz wählen können. Worin unterscheiden sich Sicherheitsbestand und Meldebestand? Der Sicherheitsbestand ist der Bestand, den Sie über den erwarteten Bedarf hinaus vorhalten – und zwar gezielt, um genau die Schwankungen abzufedern, die eine Prognose nicht vorhersagen kann. Er ist strikt vom Umlaufbestand zu trennen, also von dem Bestand, den Sie in einem normalen Wiederbeschaffungszyklus planmäßig verkaufen oder verbrauchen. Am häufigsten werden Sicherheitsbestand und Meldebestand miteinander verwechselt. Beide hängen zusammen, sind aber nicht dasselbe: Meldebestand = Erwarteter Bedarf während der Wiederbeschaffungszeit + Sicherheitsbestand Anders gesagt: Der Meldebestand sagt Ihnen, wann Sie bestellen müssen. Der Sicherheitsbestand ist das Polster, das verhindert, dass Sie leerlaufen, bevor diese Bestellung eintrifft. Wie berechnet man den Sicherheitsbestand am einfachsten? Welche Berechnung die richtige ist, hängt davon ab, wie planbar Ihr Bedarf und Ihre Wiederbeschaffungszeiten sind. Für viele Unternehmen ist die Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode ein guter Einstieg, weil sie einfach zu rechnen ist und nur grundlegende historische Daten voraussetzt. Die Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode Wenn Ihnen nur wenige historische Daten vorliegen, liefert die Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode schnell einen belastbaren Wert: Sicherheitsbestand = (Maximaler Tagesbedarf × Maximale Wiederbeschaffungszeit) − (Durchschnittlicher Tagesbedarf × Durchschnittliche Wiederbeschaffungszeit) Angenommen, von einem Teil gehen in Spitzenzeiten 25 Stück pro Tag ab, im Durchschnitt 15 Stück pro Tag, und die Wiederbeschaffungszeit beträgt maximal 14 Tage bei einem Mittelwert von 10 Tagen. Die Rechnung lautet dann (25 × 14) minus (15 × 10), also 350 minus 150, und ergibt einen Sicherheitsbestand von 200 Stück. Der Haken: Diese Methode unterstellt, dass alles gleichzeitig schiefgeht – der Bedarf erreicht seinen Höchststand, Ihr Lieferant kommt zu spät, und beides trifft im selben Wiederbeschaffungszyklus zusammen. Das kann passieren, ist aber selten. Wer den Sicherheitsbestand auf ein Szenario auslegt, das vielleicht einmal in zehn Jahren eintritt, trägt diesen Puffer das ganze Jahr über mit – und genau dort versickert Working Capital. Wie lautet die Formel für den Sicherheitsbestand bei schwankendem Bedarf? Sobald Sie über verlässliche Bedarfshistorien verfügen, können Sie sich von Worst-Case-Schätzungen lösen. Die folgende Formel bemisst den Sicherheitsbestand danach, wie stark der Bedarf im Zeitverlauf tatsächlich schwankt und welchen Servicegrad Sie erreichen wollen. Sicherheitsbestand = Z × σd × √L Die Formel wirkt einschüchternd, doch jeder Bestandteil hat eine einfache Aufgabe: • Z ist der Wert, der zu Ihrem angestrebten Servicegrad gehört (siehe Tabelle unten) • σd ist die Standardabweichung des Bedarfs, also ein Maß dafür, wie stark der Tagesbedarf um seinen Mittelwert schwankt • L ist die Wiederbeschaffungszeit, angegeben in derselben Zeiteinheit wie Ihre Bedarfsdaten Jede Erhöhung des Servicegrads erfordert einen größeren Bestandspuffer. Und dieser Zuwachs verläuft nicht proportional. Der Sprung von 90 % auf 99 % Servicegrad bedeutet nicht ein bisschen mehr Bestand – er kann den Sicherheitsbestand nahezu verdoppeln. Was ist ein Servicegrad? Der Servicegrad ist der Prozentsatz des Kundenbedarfs, den ein Unternehmen innerhalb eines Wiederbeschaffungszyklus ohne Fehlbestand bedienen will. Anders formuliert: Er beschreibt, wie häufig Sie bereit sind, einen Fehlbestand zu riskieren. Höhere Servicegrade senken das Risiko, dass Ihnen die Ware ausgeht, erfordern aber auch einen höheren Sicherheitsbestand. Der richtige Zielwert ergibt sich aus dem Vergleich der Kosten eines Fehlbestands mit den Kosten der zusätzlichen Lagerhaltung. Bei einer kritischen Produktionskomponente oder einem Topseller kann ein Servicegrad von 99 % gerechtfertigt sein, bei einem Langsamdreher dagegen nicht. Die folgende Tabelle zeigt die Z-Werte für die gängigsten Servicegrad-Ziele. Servicegrad und zugehöriger Z-Wert Servicegrad Z-Wert 90% 1,28 95% 1,65 97,5% 1,96 99% 2,33 Ein Detail führt häufiger zu Fehlern als fast alles andere: Ihre Einheiten müssen zusammenpassen. Wird die Bedarfsschwankung pro Tag gemessen, muss auch die Wiederbeschaffungszeit in Tagen angegeben werden. Wer Tagesbedarf mit monatlicher Wiederbeschaffungszeit kombiniert, bekommt keine Fehlermeldung – sondern einfach ein falsches Ergebnis. Wie berücksichtigen Sie zusätzlich schwankende Wiederbeschaffungszeiten? Der Bedarf ist nicht die einzige Unsicherheitsquelle. Lieferanten halten zugesagte Termine nicht ein, die Produktion verzögert sich, Wetterlagen bremsen den Transport und Häfen sind überlastet. Wenn auch die Wiederbeschaffungszeiten schwanken, muss Ihre Berechnung des Sicherheitsbestands dieses Risiko abbilden. Dafür gibt es zwei weitere Formeln. Wenn die Wiederbeschaffungszeit schwankt, der Bedarf aber stabil ist Sicherheitsbestand = Z × σL × Davg Auch hier ist Z der Wert, der zu Ihrem angestrebten Servicegrad gehört. σL ist die Standardabweichung der Wiederbeschaffungszeit und Davg der durchschnittliche Bedarf. Nutzen Sie diese Formel, wenn Ihr Bedarf gut planbar ist, das Lieferfenster Ihres Lieferanten dagegen nicht. Wenn Bedarf und Wiederbeschaffungszeit schwanken Das ist für die meisten SKUs das realistischste Bild – und zugleich die datenhungrigste Variante: Sicherheitsbestand = Z × √(L̄ × σd² + D̄² × σL²) Hier werden die Varianzen von Bedarf und Wiederbeschaffungszeit unter einer gemeinsamen Wurzel zusammengeführt, statt zwei separate Sicherheitsbestände zu addieren. So wird das Risiko nicht doppelt gezählt. Die Formel lohnt sich nur mit belastbaren historischen Daten zu beiden Größen, bildet dafür aber am besten ab, wie reale Lieferketten tatsächlich funktionieren. Welche Methode sollten Sie wählen? Beginnen Sie mit der einfachsten Methode, die Ihre Datenlage hergibt. Sobald sich Ihre Prognosen und Ihre Datenhistorie verbessern, können Sie zu anspruchsvolleren Formeln übergehen. Bessere Daten führen in der Regel zu einem besseren Sicherheitsbestand als der bloße Griff zur komplizierteren Gleichung. Methode Formel Geeignet für Wesentlicher Nachteil Durchschnitt-Maximum (Max. Bedarf × Max. Wiederbeschaffungszeit) − (Durchschn. Bedarf × Durchschn. Wiederbeschaffungszeit) Schnelle Schätzungen, wenig Historie Unterstellt, dass Worst-Case-Bedarf und Worst-Case-Wiederbeschaffungszeit zusammentreffen; puffert tendenziell zu hoch Bedarfsschwankung (Z-Wert) Z × σd × √L Stabile Wiederbeschaffungszeit, schwankender Bedarf Blendet das Risiko schwankender Wiederbeschaffungszeiten vollständig aus Schwankende Wiederbeschaffungszeit Z × σL × Davg Stabiler Bedarf, schwankende Wiederbeschaffungszeit Blendet das Bedarfsrisiko vollständig aus Kombiniert (doppelte Schwankung) Z × √(L̄ × σd² + D̄² × σL²) Bedarf und Wiederbeschaffungszeit schwanken beide Am genauesten, erfordert aber die umfangreichsten historischen Daten Rechenbeispiel: Eine SKU bei drei Servicegraden Nehmen Sie eine SKU mit einem durchschnittlichen Tagesbedarf von 50 Stück, einer Standardabweichung des Bedarfs von 12 Stück und einer Wiederbeschaffungszeit von 7 Tagen. Mit der Formel für Bedarfsschwankungen ergibt sich bei drei Servicegraden: • 90% Servicegrad (Z = 1,28): 1,28 × 12 × √7 ≈ 41 Stück • 95% Servicegrad (Z = 1,65): 1,65 × 12 × √7 ≈ 52 Stück • 99% Servicegrad (Z = 2,33): 2,33 × 12 × √7 ≈ 74 Stück Beachten Sie, was sich verändert hat: Der Bedarf ist exakt gleich geblieben, die Wiederbeschaffungszeit ebenfalls. Verändert hat sich einzig der Servicegrad. Genau deshalb ist die Festlegung des Servicegrads ebenso sehr eine unternehmerische wie eine mathematische Entscheidung. Wie dimensionieren Sie den Sicherheitsbestand je SKU, statt pauschal zu überpuffern? Alle SKUs gleich zu behandeln ist einer der schnellsten Wege, unnötig Kapital im Bestand zu binden. Bei manchen Produkten lässt sich ein sehr hoher Servicegrad rechtfertigen, weil ein Fehlbestand teuer ist. Bei anderen schlicht nicht. Genau hier heben viele Unternehmen verstecktes Working Capital. Laut Arda lässt sich durch die Optimierung des Sicherheitsbestands anhand tatsächlicher Bedarfsschwankungen statt anhand von Worst-Case-Annahmen der Überbestand so weit senken, dass 15–25 % des im Pufferbestand gebundenen Working Capital freigesetzt werden. Ein praxistauglicher Einstieg: 1. Klassifizieren Sie Ihre SKUs nach Umsatz- oder Margenbeitrag und danach, wie störend ein Fehlbestand wäre 2. Ordnen Sie den Klassen Servicegrade zu und reservieren Sie die höchsten Werte für die SKUs, bei denen ein Fehlbestand wirklich wehtut 3. Rechnen Sie regelmäßig nach , denn Bedarfs- und Wiederbeschaffungsmuster verschieben sich, und ein einmal jährlich festgelegter Sicherheitsbestand veraltet Häufig gestellte Fragen Sind Sicherheitsbestand und Pufferbestand dasselbe? Ja. Beide Begriffe bezeichnen zusätzlichen Bestand, der Unsicherheiten bei Bedarf und Wiederbeschaffungszeit abfedert – getrennt vom Umlaufbestand, den Sie in einer normalen Wiederbeschaffungsperiode planmäßig verbrauchen. Welche Formel für den Sicherheitsbestand sollten die meisten Unternehmen verwenden? Das hängt von der Qualität Ihrer Daten ab. Wenn Sie gerade erst beginnen, reicht die Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode in der Regel aus. Liegen verlässliche historische Bedarfsdaten vor, liefert die Formel für Bedarfsschwankungen (Z-Wert) meist ein ausgewogeneres Ergebnis. Die kombinierte Formel sollten Sie nur einsetzen, wenn Sie belastbare Daten zu Bedarfs- und Wiederbeschaffungsschwankungen haben. Wie oft sollte ich den Sicherheitsbestand neu berechnen? Überprüfen Sie ihn immer dann, wenn sich Bedarfsmuster oder Wiederbeschaffungszeiten spürbar verändern – mindestens jedoch quartalsweise. Ein einmal berechneter und nie wieder hinterfragter Wert bildet irgendwann nicht mehr ab, wie sich Ihre Lieferanten und Kunden tatsächlich verhalten. Was tun, wenn ich nicht genügend Daten habe? Fangen Sie einfach an. Wenn Ihnen nur grundlegende historische Daten vorliegen, schaffen Sie mit der Durchschnitt-Maximum-Methode eine Ausgangsbasis. Sobald Sie mehr Bedarfshistorie gesammelt haben, können Sie auf die statistischen Formeln umsteigen und den Sicherheitsbestand präziser berechnen. Braucht jede SKU denselben Servicegrad? Nein. Legen Sie Servicegrade je SKU-Klasse danach fest, wie teuer ein Fehlbestand wäre – und nicht als eine einzige Vorgabe für das gesamte Sortiment. Sie möchten bessere Eingangsdaten für Ihre Sicherheitsbestandsrechnung? Jede Formel für den Sicherheitsbestand steht und fällt mit einem Punkt: verlässlichen Daten. Ist die Bedarfshistorie lückenhaft oder sind die Wiederbeschaffungszeiten der Lieferanten veraltet, liefert auch die beste Gleichung das falsche Ergebnis. Hersteller, die Manufacturing Supply Chain von SPS Commerce nutzen, erhalten standardisierte Echtzeit-Transparenz über die Leistung ihrer Lieferanten und über eingehendes Material – und damit verlässlichere Eingangsdaten für ihre Bestandsentscheidungen.

title: Duke Energy invests $500,000 to help small businesses grow across North Carolina
summary: § Twenty nonprofits will provide microgrants and business support to hundreds of local entrepreneurs across the state § Grants are a continuation of North Carolina small businesses support, with over $3 million since 2020 Charlotte, N.C. – The Duke...
body_text: 20 nonprofits will provide microgrants and business support to hundreds of local entrepreneurs across the state Grants are a continuation of North Carolina small businesses support, with over $3 million since 2020 Charlotte, N.C. – The Duke Energy Foundation is providing $500,000 in grants to North Carolina organizations that help small businesses start, grow and thrive. Our view: “ Small businesses are woven into the fabric of our communities. They're the restaurants where neighbors gather, the childcare centers that help parents stay in the workforce and the downtown storefronts that give a town its identity," said Kendal Bowman, Duke Energy's North Carolina president. “By working through trusted partners, we're helping entrepreneurs access the resources they need to grow, create jobs and continue serving the people who depend on them every day.” Where the money goes: $25,000 grants have been awarded to 20 nonprofits that will provide microgrants to individual small businesses from the mountains to the coast. Funded projects will reflect the unique needs of local communities, such as supporting downtown revitalization and storefront improvements, helping businesses invest in equipment, technology and e-commerce capabilities or providing mentorship, technical assistance or business training. Arts Davidson County (Davidson) Asheville Downtown Association Foundation (Buncombe) Clayton Chamber Foundation (Johnston) Davidson College (Mecklenburg, Iredell, Cabarrus, Gaston, Lincoln) Davidson-Davie Community College Foundation (Davidson, Davie) Downtown Asheboro (Randolph) Downtown North Wilkesboro Partnership (Wilkes) Dunn Area Chamber Foundation (Harnett) Elevents (Henderson) Forever Bonded (Edgecombe, Wilson, Johnston, Pitt, Nash, Cumberland, New Hanover, Wake) Greater Fayetteville Chamber Foundation (Cumberland, Harnett, Hoke and surrounding counties) The Foundation of the Home Builders Association of Durham Orange & Chatham Counties (Chatham, Durham, Orange) Jacksonville Onslow Economic Development Partnership (Onslow) Montcross Tomorrow Chamber Foundation (Gaston) Partners for Children & Families (Moore) Region A Foundation (Graham, Jackson, Macon, Swain and portions of Cherokee) Reidsville Downtown Corporation (Rockingham) The Surry County Economic Development Foundation (Surry) Town of Magnolia (Duplin) Western Sampson Commerce Group (Sampson) Duke Energy Foundation The Duke Energy Foundation provides nearly $30 million annually in philanthropic support to meet the needs of communities where Duke Energy customers live and work. The Foundation is funded by Duke Energy shareholders. Duke Energy Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky. Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs. More information is available at duke-energy.com . Follow Duke Energy on X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook for stories about the people and innovations powering its communities. title: Definitive Healthcare launches early adopter program for new AI-powered healthcare intelligence platform
summary: Definitive Healthcare announces an early adopter program for its new AI-powered platform, giving select organizations early access as the company works toward general availability later this year.
body_text: Unifying claims, provider, consumer, and expert data enables organizations to uncover growth opportunities and make faster, better-informed decisions. Framingham, MA – August 6, 2026 – Definitive Healthcare (Nasdaq: DH), a provider of healthcare data and analytics, today announced an early adopter program for its new AI-powered platform, giving select organizations early access as the company works toward general availability later this year. Definitive Healthcare is advancing its AI strategy by combining its trusted healthcare data assets with conversational AI to surface insights across providers, organizations, claims, affiliations, KOLs, and consumer datasets. The platform will enable users to: Size market opportunities with confidence Optimize sales territories for maximum impact Identify and prioritize high-value prospects Surface the right decision makers faster Reduce patient leakage and strengthen networks The new platform brings together healthcare intelligence that is uniquely available in a single solution, enabling organizations to ask complex questions, understand relationships throughout the healthcare ecosystem, identify meaningful opportunities, and make faster, more informed strategic, commercial, and product development decisions. "Definitive Healthcare has been using AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics to create proprietary healthcare intelligence for years," said Srinivas Attipalli, Head of AI at Definitive Healthcare. "This platform is the next step in that journey, giving customers a new way to explore the intersections of markets, providers, organizations, patients, and the people who influence healthcare decisions." Select Definitive Healthcare customers, spanning health systems, life sciences organizations, and other industries selling into healthcare, are being invited to participate in the early adopter program beginning in August 2026. Feedback from early adopters will help shape the final product experience ahead of a planned general availability release in late 2026. Organizations interested in following the platform's progress can visit https://go.definitivehc.com/ai to learn more and stay informed about future availability. “The organizations that lead in healthcare are the ones that can identify opportunities early and act with confidence," said Tina Hannagan, Chief Commercial Officer at Definitive Healthcare. "By combining Definitive Healthcare's trusted healthcare intelligence with AI, we're helping customers move from data to decisions faster than ever before." About Definitive Healthcare Definitive Healthcare is a data and analytics company focused on the business side of healthcare. The healthcare market is complex — our data makes it clearer. title: New Weekend Editor in Metro
body_text: Robert Barba, a longtime journalist with a well of experience, is joining The Times. Read more below from Metro editors. The Metro desk prides itself on putting the “New York” in The New York Times, and if New York never sleeps, the desk shouldn’t either. As we move to strengthen our coverage of the city and region, we want to make sure that our report is as robust on Saturdays and Sundays as it is during the week. That means adding a weekend editor to our team. We are pleased to announce that Robert Barba, a longtime journalist who most recently worked as an accountability editor overseeing reporters covering Albany and the environment at WNYC and Gothamist, will step into the new role. Robert has a well of experience in breaking news and enterprise. He previously worked as spot news editor for Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal and as news editor on the U.S. news team at The Journal. He was on the team that produced The Journal’s 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre feature, which was a finalist for the 2022 Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting. “Robert is a seasoned and unflappable journalist who has worked in some of the highest pressure newsrooms,” said Andrés Martinez, deputy editor for crime and justice on Metro, who worked with Robert at The Journal. “This will make him indispensable to an ambitious weekend operation.” Beginning his journalism career as a business desk intern at The Denver Post and Boulder Daily Camera, Robert also has deep knowledge of the finance industry. He covered the 2008 financial crisis at American Banker. He remains a proponent of business journalism and is the president of the Society for Advancing Business Editing and Writing. Robert, a native of Denver, is also a lifetime member of the National Association of Hispanic Journalists. He begins on Aug. 24. — Nikita Stewart, Steve Smith, Dean Chang and Andrés Martinez
